I haven't directly or indirectly interacted with many angels--Blasphemer Amon; Calamity Queen Cohinem; the evil spirit suspected of being the Red Angel Medici; Tail Devourer Ouroboros, as described by Little Sun; Miracle Invoker Zaratul from Roselle's diaries; the Creator's son, Adam; Hermes, who hasn't been confirmed to be an angel; and the Snake of Fate Will Auceptin, who's still inside his mother's womb... Apart from the last two, the others appear extremely evil. Even the words they leave behind might drive a reader mad or make them lose control... Will my dear poet ultimately end up as a sacrifice to this angel parasite... This can explain why he thinks of himself as the protagonist of a play, the special one, and why he was willing to help me hide my secret... The Zoroast family controls the Marauder pathway, which can steal the Beyonder powers of others. That's why Leonard was able to find and participate in the gathering of the Hermits of Fate... It's no wonder he offered to use Blood Vessel Thief--it's because he has a Grandpa to help him. He was able to instantly steal Megose's most potent power... Heh, what Hermits of Fate? They're just a bunch of thieves and frauds. At best, the targets of their theft and fraud are time and fate... In short, my dear poet's Grandpa isn't a good person. I have to find a chance to warn him... But therein lies the problem: they're always together. Any warning will only hasten the danger. Klein's thoughts raced, but he ultimately found no workable solution. He could only set the matter aside for the moment and plan to ask Mr. Azik and the Snake of Mercury, Will Auceptin, whether they knew what to do. During those few minutes, he even considered using Blasphemer Amon. Simply put, he would divulge to the Creator's son that an angel from the Zoroast family resided in Leonard Mitchell's body, prompting "Him" to "eat" the parasite. According to what Klein knew, the Amon family supported the Tudor Empire during the Fourth Epoch, while the Zoroast family belonged to the Solomon Empire, making the two enemies. Furthermore, according to the Law of Beyonder Characteristics Conservation, powerhouses from the same pathway would have greater conflicts the higher their Sequence was. This was akin to the battle between the two Snakes of Mercury. Unfortunately, reality constrained this solution, so Klein ultimately abandoned it. First, he didn't know where to find Blasphemer Amon. Second, he feared that a battle between angels would directly destroy Leonard Mitchell. Third, a powerful Amon might create an even worse problem. I'll first have Emlyn attempt the transaction and observe the situation. I can decide what to do when I know more... Klein reined in his thoughts and said to the radio transceiver connected to Arrodes, "Ask your question." The radio transceiver clacked with increasing briskness as it gently fed out illusory white paper. "No, there's no need. "This is an addendum to my question which doesn't need to abide by the rules. "Great Master, I sense a special item outside your room, but I am unable to see through it. Can you tell me what it is?" This magic mirror is impressive. It seems able to see everything. It only suffers interference when dealing with high-level matters, as though they're obscured by a mosaic... Klein calmly replied, "The Die of Probability." Amid the tapping, Arrodes presented new words on the illusory white paper. "So it's that thing... Great Master, you can ask your question." Klein thought for a moment before saying, "What do you have to mention regarding the Die of Probability?" At that moment, the radio transceiver seemed to brighten and no longer looked as gloomy as before. The speed at which it spewed out illusory white paper slowed. "It's a fellow that's especially petty and bears grudges. Master, you have to quickly give it to someone else! "It's an item formed from the Uniqueness of the Wheel of Fortune pathway. You can give it to any other Snake of Fate, and 'They' will be very grateful. In short, it isn't suitable to be your servant. "The aura is dissipating. Your loyal and humble servant, Arrodes, has no choice but to leave. Finally, let me praise you once again, my Great Master, the ruler above the spirit world. Bye bye~" Uniqueness... The Die of Probability is actually the Uniqueness of the Monster pathway... This is the first time I've encountered a so-called Uniqueness. Something capable of digitizing the entire real world truly is terrifying... The Monster pathway is also called the Wheel of Fortune pathway. Is Sequence 0 Wheel of Fortune? Klein looked at the radio transceiver, which had returned to normal, and temporarily reined in his thoughts. He felt no greed toward the Die of Probability. It didn't belong to the Seer pathway and carried terrifying negative effects. He also feared that, given time, this vindictive die would draw Tail Devourer Ouroboros to him. Even if this thing can be isolated and sealed when placed above the gray fog, there's a high chance of it digitizing the entire mysterious space. In the future, the Tarot Gatherings might end up becoming a tabletop role-playing game... Klein had never come into contact with items of this level before, so he was unable to determine what would happen if he were to throw the Die of Probability above the gray fog. He decided to continue intimidating the die and safely deliver it to Oravi Island, where members of the Life School of Thought would have the means to seal it. He didn't mind that the mission's difficulty exceeded the payment he would receive, because the greatest benefit he would gain was the friendship of the Snake of Fate Will Auceptin. Backlund, Harvest Church. Emlyn White held a strange badge which was the size of an eyeball and chuckled inwardly. The World certainly is long-winded. I'm only looking for a Nighthawk named Leonard Mitchell on Pinster Street in North Borough, aren't I? He even went out of his way to emphasize that the man has a secret and will probably pull me into a dream. This is showing doubt in my abilities! Emlyn stood up and changed into a tailcoat and white shirt. He then turned his head to look out the window. Heh heh, he has a secret, while I have mine. I dare bet that Lord Nibbs or the other Earls are secretly watching me. If anything happens, they will definitely help me to some extent... Being pulled into a dream... Emlyn contemplated for a few seconds before using spiritually rich materials to concoct a blue medicine. Putting away the bottle and the remaining ingredients, he picked up a silk top hat and walked out of the break room. After bidding farewell to Bishop Utravsky, he left the Harvest Church. It was still morning, but Backlund's sky was gloomy. There was a faint fog that spread like water. Emlyn narrowed his eyes, put on his hat, and murmured, "The sunlight is a little dazzling..." He hailed a rental carriage and went straight for the steam metro station. He spent six pence on a first-class ticket to North Borough. This saved him far more time than traveling there directly! About forty minutes later, he arrived at his destination and stood outside the door of 7 Pinster Street. Emlyn politely rang the doorbell and patiently waited for a minute. Just as he was about to write a note and slip it through the gap beneath the door to arrange another time, he heard languid footsteps approach. Doesn't sound like a servant... Emlyn gave an almost imperceptible nod, took out the medicine he had prepared, and drained it in one smooth motion. Then, he watched the door open and saw a black-haired, green-eyed man appear before him. He was dressed in home wear--a white shirt and black trousers. His shirt was untucked, allowing it to flutter gently in the wind. Amidst his suaveness were hints of uninhibited freedom. Although he's a believer of Evernight, I have to say that his looks are barely comparable to those of us Sanguine... Emlyn took off his hat and gently raised his chin. "Good morning, are you Mr. Leonard Mitchell?" Leonard frowned almost imperceptibly at the handsome, red-eyed gentleman. He raised a hand to cover his mouth and yawned indifferently. "You are?" "A visitor. I have something I would like to seek your help on." Emlyn didn't reveal his identity as he smiled with a rather obvious arrogance. This attitude gave Leonard a baffling sense of familiarity. It was as though he had seen his former self--the person who always thought of himself as being the most special, the protagonist of this era. He cleared his throat and said, "I'm only an ordinary citizen. I do not accept missions. "If you have any issues, then you can find a private detective." Emlyn White smiled and said, "This matter is something only you can complete." He looked to his sides and continued, "I wish to purchase a mystical item that can steal the Beyonder powers of others." Leonard's eyes focused as he asked in a deep voice, "Who are you?" At that moment, Emlyn didn't answer immediately. Instead, he surveyed his surroundings and clicked his tongue with a smile. "Impressive. I nearly failed to realize that I had been pulled into a dream." He wasn't in a rush to leave as he took out the small badge he received from The World in front of Leonard Mitchell's solemn expression. Leonard took a glance as his expression eased slightly. He cocked his head slightly and paused for a few seconds. In silence, Emlyn White watched the scene around him fracture and vanish like broken glass. Leonard sneered and pointed inside the house. "Let's talk inside."
Chapter 610: Throwing the Die At Leonard Mitchell's invitation, Emlyn showed no fear. Top hat in hand and a faint smile on his lips, he entered the house without hesitation. He didn't remove his coat, for a Potions Professor often carried numerous supplementary items, and the sight beneath his carefully arranged concealment would be anything but elegant. Emlyn sat with his starched tailcoat immaculate, leaned leisurely against the backrest, and said, "Actually, there's no need to go to such trouble. "If you have it, name the price; otherwise, say so frankly." "Of course, I'm very certain you have one." He chuckled, his bright red eyes reflecting Leonard Mitchell's carelessly dressed figure. Knowing that Leonard had a secret while Leonard knew nothing about him delighted Emlyn and filled him with an intense sense of superiority. Leonard combed his fingers through his raven-black hair and casually sat opposite Emlyn. Showing neither panic nor confusion, he smiled. "At the very least, I need to know who wants it." "Perhaps I do, or perhaps a friend does." Emlyn raised his chin and smiled faintly. Leonard squinted his eyes as he cocked his head, as though in thought. Finally, he laughed. "Alright, since you've already taken out that badge, I'll answer you frankly. "I do have a mystical item that can be used to steal the Beyonder powers of others, but I only have that one item. "If you wish to buy it, 7,000 pounds. No negotiation." 7,000 pounds? A mystical item of this kind is that expensive? Although he didn't have to pay for it, Emlyn was still shocked. He nearly failed to maintain his bearing as a Sanguine. He automatically converted that sum into the number of dolls and doll dresses it could buy. After two seconds of thought, Emlyn revealed a smile and said, "I'll consider it. I'll answer you in two days." "Sure." Leonard curled the corners of his lips. After leaving 7 Pinster Street, Emlyn calmly hired a rental carriage to the North Borough steam metro station, then returned to the bridge in South Borough. Removing his hat, Emlyn glanced back at the street, where carriages and pedestrians passed to and fro. He chuckled and stepped into the Harvest Church. In between a tree and a black street lamp, an inconspicuous shadow suddenly moved, revealing the black-haired, green-eyed Leonard Mitchell. His appearance was silent, but it didn't garner the attention of any pedestrians. "Someone from the Church of Earth Mother?" Leonard frowned slightly as he muttered to himself. He paused for two seconds before leaving Rose Street where the Harvest Church was situated. 7,000 pounds? Why doesn't he just go rob a bank? Above the gray fog, Klein, who had received the feedback from Emlyn, nearly blurted out. As Gehrman Sparrow, he had previously said something similar, but the circumstances and his mood were completely different. Using the bounty on the Golden Dream's third mate, Flowery Bow Tie Jodeson, as a reference, Klein estimated that a similar mystical item was worth about 5,000 pounds. Even with a premium, the price should have topped out at 6,000. Yet Leonard Mitchell had demanded 7,000 pounds outright! Could it be an item left behind by a High-Sequence Beyonder, with stealing Beyonder powers as only one of its effects? No, if that were true, its price would start at 10,000 pounds... My dear poet, I never knew you were such a profiteer. You always seemed so carefree and indifferent to money... Klein couldn't help sighing. Since he had a clue and a glimmer of hope, and the problem could be resolved with money, Klein didn't wish to seek out other channels and risk a mishap. He quickly calculated his wealth and discovered that it was an acceptable price. Including the 300-pound advance from the Apothecary, the 5,400-pound bounty for Wormtongue, and the cash I got from the bodies, then subtracting the 200 pounds to be paid to Miss Magician, I have a total of 12,767 pounds in cash and 5 gold coins. This doesn't include my 3 soli and 8 pence in change. In addition, Miss Justice will pay the 2,000 pounds she owes me before the end of the week, as well as the 1,800 pounds for the Psychiatrist characteristic. I'm actually richer than I thought I was. Even in Backlund, I can be considered a tycoon. Klein inhaled and didn't hesitate any further. He made the cash fly out from the junk pile and land on the table. He carefully counted out 7,500 pounds in cash and set it aside--7,000 pounds for the mystical item and 500 pounds for Emlyn's "hazard pay." Sigh, after all the effort it took to surpass ten thousand, more than half of it will be gone in an instant... Klein conjured The World in a praying posture to inform Emlyn that there was no problem with proceeding with the transaction. Fifteen minutes later, Emlyn was to hold a ritual to receive Mr. Fool's bestowment. In addition, Klein had The World warn Emlyn not to rush to complete the deal after receiving the cash. He had to wait until tomorrow. Klein feared that the angel from the Zoroast family inside Leonard Mitchell would sense the gray fog's aura on the money. He wanted to let it "air out," just as he had when giving Emlyn the badge. Fifteen minutes later, Klein glanced at the cash pile which had shrunk by more than half and sighed before returning to the real world. It was already 10:40 on Friday morning. They were about eight hours from Oravi Island. It's time to intimidate the Die of Probability again... Klein muttered, held the ritual, and brought out the iron cigar case which contained the All-Black Eye. He guessed that Darkwill would suspect something, so he deliberately took the die into the washroom to deal with it. Once the Die of Probability had calmed again, Klein quickly put away the All-Black Eye and iron cigar case. He breathed a long sigh of relief and silently calculated the time. It should be enough to last until Darkwill hands it to the contact. There's no need to deal with it again. With this in mind, Klein began to consider another problem with a certain degree of concern. The All-Black Eye has appeared before the True Creator, and it bears "His" mental corruption. Taking it out every few hours might allow "Him" to lock onto me and send powerhouses to find me. However, it was exposed for only a minute or two each time, so the problem shouldn't be too serious. Even if "He" senses it, "His" estimate of the area won't be very precise. Sigh, when the True Creator is involved, divination can't provide an answer. I can only remain vigilant. Thankfully, this is the last time, and only about eight hours remain before we reach our destination... Why am I raising flags for myself? Ptooey! Ptooey! Ptooey! I wasn't thinking anything! Klein picked up the Die of Probability and returned to the living room, where he saw the chubby Apothecary slumped in the reclining chair, looking completely exhausted. The owl Harry, by contrast, brimmed with energy, as though it needed no rest. Are these the different traits that different creatures gain from taking the same potion? At the very least, Miss Justice has never mentioned that she doesn't need sleep... Is this a unique trait arising from an owl's physiology? Sigh, I don't know much about owls. Indeed, I'm just a keyboard warrior and a jack of all trades... Klein sat on the sofa, placed the milky-white die in the ring box, and patiently waited for evening, when the ship was scheduled to dock. Time ticked by as the sun gradually set in the west. Klein, whose eyes had been closed, suddenly sat upright. He sensed an extreme danger descending upon the area! It had exceeded a Seer's spiritual intuition and the Clown's intuition for danger. It seemed to stem from the formless gray fog which strangely rippled around him. An enemy! Tail Devourer Ouroboros or the Aurora Order's Saint? Klein opened his eyes as he began considering countermeasures with an abnormally serious expression. Any mistake at a time like this would force him to contemplate resurrection. As for Darkwill and Harry, there was absolutely no way for them to be spared! At first, he hoped the visitor could sense only a vague general area and might not find him or the Die of Probability. However, considering that he was aboard an isolated ship at sea, it wouldn't be too difficult to lock onto the target. Once that happened, the situation would only worsen, leaving surrender as the only choice. Above the liner, space was suddenly torn open as an invisible door filled with complicated symbols appeared. Two pale hands reached through the door and pulled sharply backward, allowing the man's entire body to emerge. He wore a black bonnet and a traditional dark robe favored by the elderly, yet he appeared no older than forty. His slightly curled brown hair looked unnaturally stiff. Countless illusory images flitted through his dark eyes, as though layer upon layer of chaotic worlds lay hidden within. As Klein's sense of danger intensified, just the change in his expression frightened Darkwill and Harry enough for them to freeze. Without hesitation, he followed the plans he had made for such situations. He leaned forward and picked up the Die of Probability. "Determine the fate of the malefic visitor who just arrived. I want a one!" Klein commanded in a deep, soft voice as he threw the milky-white die. He instinctively prayed to the Goddess, hoping the recently intimidated die would remain obedient and honor the rule he had declared. Meanwhile, he appeared extremely calm to prevent the die from sensing his anxiety and seizing the opportunity to cause trouble. The Die of Probability rolled several times with a series of clinks, then settled with the blood-red one facing upward. Above the liner, the black-robed man, who looked no older than forty, had the entire ship reflected in his eyes. He emanated his spirituality and scanned the surroundings. Extending a hand, he grasped the space before him and suddenly pulled open a nearly invisible door. The powerhouse stepped in and vanished from the spot. Inside the first-class cabin, Klein immediately felt the danger distancing itself from him. He couldn't help but heave a sigh of relief. He looked at the Die of Probability on the coffee table and couldn't help but sigh inwardly. If this die didn't have such a negative side effect and could be utilized to its full extent, it would be a divine artifact! As expected of a Grade 0 Sealed Artifact. As expected of the Uniqueness of the Monster pathway... Only then did Darkwill recover enough courage to ask cautiously, "W-what just happened?" Klein maintained his posture and calmly replied, "There's no need for you to know." "I understand, I understand. The more I know, the greater the danger I'll be in." Darkwill wiped the cold sweat from his face. There were no further accidents over the next few hours. After the sun sank below the horizon and the sky grew completely dark, Klein finally saw a towering lighthouse appear nearby.
Chapter 611: Fate Councilor Oravi lay northeast of the Rorsted Archipelago. The straight-line distance wasn't great, but the safe sea route forced ships to make numerous detours, adding several hundred nautical miles to the journey. It had originally been a primitive island, uninhabited by humans and home to many kinds of Beyonder creatures. After the hunting era ended, the Loen Kingdom exiled certain criminals there, and villages and towns gradually appeared across Oravi Island. As more islands to the east were discovered and colonized, Oravi's convenient position along the sea route and wealth of natural resources attracted many new immigrants, turning it into a thriving port. The lighthouse shone warmly through the darkness, guiding liners into the harbor to dock. "We've finally arrived. My thanks to the crimson moon and fate for their blessings." Darkwill jumped from the last gangway and landed on solid concrete. To be precise, apart from fate, you should thank The Fool and Sea God for their blessings... Klein held his leather suitcase with one hand as he tapped his cane. Darkwill carefully put away the ring box containing the Die of Probability, then immediately asked where Carnot the bellman lived. He hired a carriage and went straight to St. Draco Cathedral, where he entered the magnificent bell tower with its bold red, blue, and yellow decoration. Inside the bell tower, Carnot had a cramped room he could call his own. Knock! Knock! Knock! Darkwill knocked on the door thrice, eager to hand over the item on his person. With a creak, the brown wooden door opened, and a large, slightly hunched man emerged. He appeared to be in his forties. None of his facial features looked strange on its own, yet together they formed a deeply discordant whole. One glance was enough for Klein to notice that his eyes weren't level and his nostrils differed in size. The muscles on the left side of his face sagged slightly, pulling down the corner of his mouth, while the right side was the exact opposite. Carnot's legs were plainly different lengths, and one arm was thick while the other was thin. His entire body was badly disproportionate, making him extremely ugly. "Who are you?" Dressed in a black robe, Carnot glanced at the duo. "Are you the bellman, Carnot?" Darkwill asked cautiously. Carnot chuckled, one corner of his mouth rising while the other remained low. "There shouldn't be a second person as ugly as me." "Indeed." Darkwill nodded with complete honesty, then laughed. "I can tell you have a healthy frame of mind. To be honest, a man's looks don't matter. What matters is his skill in bed." Tsk, that's because you've never met women obsessed with handsome faces... Having lived through the age of mass celebrity, Klein scoffed inwardly. Carnot's expression darkened as he said, "I don't wish to discuss such matters." "You have problems in that area? No problem. I have all kinds of medicine that can cure them..." Before Darkwill could finish, Klein stepped forward, afraid he would be beaten to death. He put half his body between them as he said in a deep voice, "He's Roy King's student." "I figured. Roy King once described his traits." Carnot made way and invited the two in. His room was extremely tiny, with only a single bed and a cabinet that doubled as a dining table. The washroom was at the bottom of the bell tower. Darkwill pulled out a ring box and handed it to Carnot as he forced a smile. "My teacher got me to hand this item to you." Carnot glanced at it and was visibly relieved to see four pips. He said to Darkwill, "You aren't as unreliable as your teacher made you sound. I can tell you didn't try to use it. That would've awakened it and made it realize it was no longer sealed." The chubby Apothecary flushed and admitted honestly, "That's only because it's relatively quiet right now. In another hour or two, it'll roll itself automatically. You'd better find a way to seal it again." Carnot's face twitched. "Again?" "W-well, I accidentally dropped it on the ground, and then i-it came alive..." Darkwill wanted to glance at his owl, Harry, but realized it hadn't followed him in. It was perched outside the bell tower, serving as a sentry. Carnot's eyes clearly widened as his hunched back nearly straightened. "How did you arrive here?" As far as he was concerned, Roy King's student should have died at the die's whims long ago. Darkwill hurriedly pointed to Gehrman Sparrow and said, "It's all thanks to this gentleman. He's a powerful adventurer. He provided the most effective protection and a temporary method of sealing the die." "What method?" Carnot blurted out. Klein laughed and replied, "Trade secret." Carnot's expression changed a few times as he pressed his hand to his chest and bowed. "On behalf of my organization, I thank you for your help." Darkwill continued, "Hiring him cost 1,000 pounds and the fulfillment of a request. He wants help finding a mystical item with powerful offensive abilities but no severe negative effects. He'll buy it at a reasonable price. "Uh, I only had about 300 pounds, so that was all I could pay. I'll have to rely on you to pay the rest..." Carnot fell silent as the corners of his lips twitched. "I only have about 100 pounds..." The bellman's room fell silent. Wind slipped through the cracks and brushed the three men's faces. Finally, Carnot spoke again. "Perhaps Councilor Ricciardo has the money. I'll lead you to him." From the looks of it, he trusts us. After all, a Fate Councilor is in no way comparable to a Die of Probability. If there were really problems with us, there would be no need for us to bring the die over to prevent any accidents and snatch away the Uniqueness... Klein watched as Carnot picked up a lantern from the corner of the room. At that moment, he secretly activated his Spirit Vision and swept his gaze over the man. Klein nearly raised his eyebrows. Carnot's aura colors were highly unusual. His emotional colors were perfectly ordinary, but the Ether Body representing his physical form appeared unnatural. His heart was green, his head purple, and his digestive system yellow. They resembled disparate parts mashed together in profound disharmony. Carnot's soul gave him the same impression. A monster stitched together internally? Klein made a rough judgment based on what he knew. After Carnot got the lantern, he turned his head to glance at the adventurer, Gehrman Sparrow, and said without much of an expression, "I'm very sensitive to Spirit Vision. "I believe you've noticed certain problems. I wasn't born naturally. I'm a product of the Church of Earth Mother's attempts to refine the human body. I'm considered a failed specimen, which is why I lack ability in that regard." His final sentence was directed at Darkwill. Carnot didn't speak again as he carried the lantern and donned a black robe. He hunched his huge body and used the dim light to walk down the stairs of the dark and silent bell tower. A product of the Church of Earth Mother's attempts to refine the human body? But St. Draco Cathedral belongs to the Church of Storms... Since he's a failed specimen, they paid him no further attention. Did Carnot turn his back on the Church of Earth Mother and join the Life School of Thought? That would be understandable. Both the Church of Earth Mother and the Life School of Thought possess the Apothecary pathway, so their interests must overlap... But why would the Life School of Thought send this fellow, who seems far from simple, to serve as a bellman in the Church of Storms? Is it merely an ordinary disguise, or is there a particular connection between the two? Seemingly calm, Klein followed Carnot out of the bell tower and around to a stone bridge. Just as he came close to the left side of the bridge, Klein suddenly felt something as he looked diagonally upwards. The owl, Harry, had flown out as well and landed on a tree branch. Kacha! The branch suddenly snapped, sending Harry plummeting. The owl barely managed to take flight again before hitting the ground. Darkwill was just about to say something when Carnot explained in a deep voice, "Councilor Ricciardo is injured, so his powers are somewhat out of control. Once anyone enters a specific range, they will be tainted with bad luck." Carnot stopped and threw the ring box containing the die under the bridge. "Mr. Councilor, Roy King's student has delivered the die." "Very good." A hoarse voice sounded from deep within the bridge's belly. A silver-scaled palm reached from the darkness and pinned the ring box where it had fallen in the mud. He opened the ring box and removed the milky-white die. His other silver-scaled hand emerged holding a paper-thin object made of leather. The object resembled a water pipe whose ends had been joined. It appeared grayish-white beneath the crimson moonlight. Its surface bore many intricate symbols and markings, along with numerous words in Hermes that pointed to the Snake of Mercury, Will Auceptin. Fate Councilor Ricciardo pulled the item apart and stuffed the Die of Probability into it before connecting the two ends together. Using a small-scale cycle of fate to seal the Die of Probability, keeping it perpetually dormant or calm? The Snake of Mercury, Will Auceptin, truly foresaw this situation and made preparations... Klein withdrew his gaze in relief as Ricciardo's hoarse voice rang out. "I already know of your agreement, Mr. Gehrman Sparrow. "I will help you find the mystical item after I've recovered. "As for the 700 pounds... I'll immediately augment you with good luck. Go to the few casinos in Oravi and make some bets and you'll receive the corresponding reward. Remember, do not win more than 200 pounds at each casino. You must not win more than 700 pounds in total." Which is to say that you don't have the money either... Seeing how you're hiding while injured, it's considered normal not to have money with you... Klein nodded indiscernibly and said, "Okay." He waited for about ten seconds without sensing anything. Councilor Ricciardo heaved a sigh of relief and said, "You have become sufficiently lucky." Is that so? Klein chose to believe him and didn't interrupt Darkwill as he reported his teacher's imprisonment to a senior member of the organization. Following Carnot's directions, he found a nearby casino and sat at a blackjack table. After about ten minutes, he walked out of the casino with a blank look. Not only had he failed to win, but he had lost a total of 30 pounds! What happened to the good luck? Why did I believe him? That darn old man is terrible... Klein didn't hesitate to return to the stone bridge and approached its belly. "So soon? You have pretty good luck." Ricciardo laughed and coughed beneath the dark bridge. By then, Darkwill and Harry had already found rooms at a nearby inn. Klein replied without a change in expression, "I lost." "Lost..." Ricciardo pondered the word, unable to formulate a sentence for a long time. In the darkness, an ordinary owl flew over nervously.
Chapter 612: In Hand The two streetlamps flanking the stone bridge silently illuminated the road but couldn't dispel the darkness beneath it. Only the crimson moon high above shed a faint light on the brown earth. Hidden beneath the bridge, Fate Councilor Ricciardo remained silent for so long that Klein wondered if his severe injuries had killed him. He suspected they were largely responsible for the failed luck augmentation. Just as Klein was about to ask a probing question, Ricciardo coughed and said in a deep, hoarse voice, "You live up to your reputation as a powerful adventurer capable of temporarily sealing the die... "What happened exceeded my expectations. Ahem, I'm very curious why my luck augmentation failed on you. "I regret that I can't come out to meet you in person. Otherwise, I should be able to see what Beyonders of other pathways would struggle to perceive, even with relatively powerful Spirit Vision. "That is the Fate pathway's unique advantage." So the problem lies with me? That's not the point. The point is that you need to reimburse me 700 pounds--No, 730 pounds... Klein cursed as he couldn't help but recall the orphan, Ademisaul, who had the nickname of Monster in Tingen City. The young man who was equal to half a Sequence 9 had cried out after seeing Klein before falling to the ground. His eyes bled, and the fear he exhibited was as if he had seen a devil. Because of the Wheel of Fortune pathway's unique divinity, he saw that something was wrong with me. Did he see something related to the gray fog? Unfortunately, this Fate Councilor is badly injured and surrounded by a domain of misfortune. There's no way for him to examine me... I should ask the Snake of Fate, Will Auceptin, when I return. Perhaps he knows something. However, this pathway does have the air of a charlatan. He might not answer me directly and will likely respond in vague terms... Klein remained expressionless and asked, "Then what do you plan to do?" Ricciardo sighed and said, "Get Darkwill here. I'll augment him with good luck and get him to win the money at the casinos on your behalf." Using the name of the inn Councilor Ricciardo gave, Klein quickly found the chubby Apothecary, Darkwill. Then, while carrying the suitcase and cane, Klein watched as he kept winning money at the major casinos. By midnight, he had already won 750 pounds. After receiving the remaining 730 pounds, Klein realized a problem. The luck augmentation had failed because of him! Why? Klein clutched his bulging wallet and frowned in thought. He soon thought of the thin, invisible grayish-white fog surrounding him and realized the reason. After advancing to Faceless, the gray fog has integrated with reality to a certain extent. Not only can it shield me from ravings that aren't too powerful, but it can also negate influences that alter my fate to a certain degree? Is that why this councilor's luck augmentation was ineffective? According to this logic, bad luck to a certain extent shouldn't affect me either. Heh, what the heck? It keeps me from becoming some unlucky fool, but it also destroys my chances of becoming a lucky winner... Klein secretly shook his head and followed Darkwill and the owl back to the stone bridge. He told Ricciardo how to summon his messenger and asked him to send word immediately if he learned of a mystical item with powerful offensive abilities. Afterward, Klein found an inn in Oravi's port city and rented a simple room. Backlund, morning. Beneath his beloved gloomy sky, Emlyn White walked through fog that, though thick, couldn't compare to that of November or December. Once again, he arrived outside 7 Pinster Street in the North Borough. After pulling the doorbell, he straightened his back as he lifted his chin and waited patiently. When Leonard opened the door, he looked at the handsome but detestable face before making way and allowing the visitor to enter. He was still dressed in a white shirt and black trousers, but now wore a dark vest over them. "Have you considered the matter?" Leonard asked with a smile. "No problem." Since it wasn't his money, Emlyn had no intention of haggling. He even suspected that Leonard would probably raise the price if he tried. Leonard gently nodded and smiled. "You're very rich." I can tell that you're trying to lead me to say more... Emlyn silently scoffed and replied, "That's not something you need to concern yourself with." With that said, he raised the suitcase in his hand and opened it, revealing 7,000 pounds in cash. Leonard removed the stacks of cash one by one and inspected them carefully. Then, he pulled off the red glove he wore on his left hand and handed it to Emlyn. "This is the mystical item you require. It can change colors to disguise itself. "It's called Tinder. It enhances the wearer's charm, lending his words great persuasive power. It can steal a Beyonder power from a target within 50 meters. The better you understand the target, the easier it is to steal the power you want. The less you know, the more random the result, leaving it to luck. "When the target is at Sequence 6, there is a chance of failure. The higher the Sequence, the higher the chance of failure. "Once the theft succeeds, the target loses that Beyonder power for at least twelve hours, while Tinder's owner can use it proficiently for ten minutes. "It's expensive because it has very few negative effects." Emlyn, who silently took in the introduction, had his interest piqued by a mystical item like Tinder. He asked, "What are its negative side effects?" Leonard ran a hand through his hair and smiled. "First, when wearing it, there is a small probability of losing something on you. Second, when using it, a particular Beyonder power belonging to you will be lost for at least twelve hours, but during this period, it will be the only Beyonder power lost. In other words, even if it's used repeatedly, there will only be one power lost the entire time." "Compared to the many Sealed Artifacts I know of, its negative side effects are indeed trivial." Emlyn cleared his throat as he nodded. He received Tinder and checked it carefully before taking out the stacks of cash from the suitcase and placing them on the coffee table. He then placed the glove in the suitcase rather than carrying it openly. With the suitcase, Emlyn returned to the Harvest Church just like he did before. Once he entered the priest's break room, he set up a Sacrificial ritual. The illusory and mysterious door opened as the red glove tore through the dark and deep void as it was sent directly above the gray fog. At the moment the gray fog made contact with the glove, a tiny, distorted, terrifying face suddenly appeared. It kept evaporating as it struggled to sustain itself. Klein wasn't surprised by this scene. After all, Grandpa, who resided in Leonard's body, was an angel of the Marauder pathway. If Amon could do it, "He" was almost certainly capable of doing the same. Klein had made ample preparations for this. He believed that even if Grandpa had truly reached Amon's level, he could erase the corresponding aura without allowing him to sense the gray fog or prompting him to take action against Emlyn. Picking up the Sea God Scepter, which had long been placed before him, Klein raised it commandingly and made all the blue "gems" light up at once. Suddenly, silver light bloomed above the gray fog. Lightning imbued with some of the gray fog's power descended like a storm, striking the tiny illusory face. The face dissipated completely before it could even cry out, leaving behind a dead translucent worm with twelve transparent rings. Worm of Time... but it seems weaker than Amon's... Klein muttered as he beckoned, making the red glove and peculiar worm fly toward him. After some serious scrutiny, he confirmed that the worm was basically identical to the one Amon's avatar had left behind. My dear poet's Grandpa is at the same Sequence as Amon? Sequence 1? No, not necessarily. Perhaps this is a unique trait of one of the preceding Sequences... If--if it's really a Sequence 1, the notion that Amon is the son of the Creator and a King of Angels makes it possible that he has fused with the Uniqueness or has another Sequence 1 characteristic... Klein made a guess, but he was unable to verify it. Lacking the relevant knowledge, he could only toss it into the junk pile, uncertain what the dead Worm of Time could be used for or when its spirituality would completely dissipate. 7 Pinster Street, Backlund. Leonard Mitchell sat on the sofa with his eyes tightly closed and his legs propped on the coffee table, as though trying to make up for an entire sleepless night with a brief nap. After an unknown length of time, he suddenly opened his eyes and asked in a low voice, "What happened? Have you determined the true buyer of Tinder?" An elderly voice rang out in his mind. "The aura I left behind has been eliminated, completely eliminated." "Did you discover anything?" Leonard retracted his feet as he asked in a deep voice. The ancient voice sighed. "Nothing. "Everything was over before I could react. "If I were in my best condition, I might've grasped the relevant clues. Unfortunately, I've remained weak for years." Leonard remained silent for more than ten seconds before he shook his head. "Then we'll temporarily treat it as if this never happened." Above the gray fog, Klein listened to Emlyn's report and took note of the information regarding the mystical item. He fiddled with the glove named Tinder as he examined it. "Heh heh, this way, I'll have a glove for my right hand," he chuckled to himself. After careful consideration, Klein abandoned the idea of immediately extracting the True Creator's mental corruption from the All-Black Eye. To maximize his chances of success, he decided to save the opportunity for when he concocted the Marionettist potion. According to the City of Silver's records, such a procedure posed no problems even without the gray fog's protection. With the gray fog, there should be no additional accidents, even when dealing with mental corruption left behind by the True Creator. I can also use Tinder normally. Yes, when I need it, I'll have to leave my cash, pocket watch, and other mystical items above the gray fog. I mustn't let anything get lost... In fact, even if I don't, it won't be a serious problem. I'm a Seer. Do I need to fear being unable to find something I've lost? Heh heh. In an ordinary battle, I'll have Creeping Hunger on my left hand and Tinder on my right. The thought alone is formidable... Klein reined in his thoughts and discovered that everything related to the Sequence 5 Marionettist potion was ready, apart from the two commonly seen supplementary ingredients. He nodded indiscernibly and muttered silently to himself, I just need to wait for the Faceless potion to be completely digested! Then I'll board a ship belonging to the Admiral of Stars or The Hanged Man and head east of the Sonia Sea to find mermaids.
Chapter 613: Leonard's Investigation Loen Kingdom, East Chester County, Stoen City. Having left the manor, Audrey moved into a villa. After she finished engaging in social gatherings with the local nobles, she sent her servant to the Varvat Bank to withdraw a sum of cash. She didn't need to worry about this any further. She could easily pay off the 2,000 pounds she owed Mr. Fool's Blessed, and she could also pay the 1,800 pounds she owed Mr. World for the Psychiatrist characteristic. Fifteen minutes later, Audrey opened her bedroom door and glanced at her personal maid, Annie, who was supervising the other servants. She looked down at the golden retriever sitting beside the wall and smiled. Lowering her voice, she asked with shining eyes, "Susie, you'll receive a gift soon. Are you looking forward to it?" If it were in the past, Audrey would've definitely said, "Susie, your present is here," making the golden retriever realize that she could find the actual item in the room as well. Otherwise, it was very easy for Susie, who had been studying the basics of mysticism, to guess that Audrey had used ritualistic magic. With this new phrasing, Audrey could later claim to have received a mysterious letter or news in her bedroom confirming that the gift was about to be delivered. That left far too many possibilities for Susie to guess the truth. Susie could perceive the joy and sincerity deep in Audrey's heart. She instinctively opened her mouth, hoping to stir the air and produce a voice. She wanted to ask about the gift, but keenly sensed Audrey's personal maid, Annie, approaching. The alert Susie abandoned the idea. She returned to the state of being an ordinary dog as she slowly wagged her tail to express her joy and anticipation. After making an excuse to head out, Audrey entered a "chemistry laboratory" that she had specially marked out for herself. She placed the Psychiatrist characteristic and supplementary ingredients on the table. "Susie, do you still remember the potion-concocting process?" She cleared her throat and straightened her back as she excitedly played the role of a teacher. "Woof, I remember!" Susie already knew what her present was. In her joy, she barked. Audrey added, "Try to concoct it by yourself." Susie looked down at her paws and suddenly fell silent. Audrey was taken aback before a brief silence ensued. A few seconds later, before the golden retriever could speak, Audrey covered her mouth as naturally as possible and giggled. "Alright, Susie, there's no need to say anything. I know what you mean. You're only a dog and can't concoct the potion, right?" How embarrassing... At the same time, Audrey, who wore a charming and graceful external bearing, facepalmed herself inwardly. "Woof!" Susie nodded forcefully. Audrey took the opportunity and turned around. Soon, she finished concocting the Psychiatrist potion. She had previously asked Susie and learned that she had already finished digesting the potion on Wednesday. That's less than two months... Yes, a large part of the reason is that no one pays attention to Susie. She can roam anywhere in the manor or villa and eavesdrop, allowing her to discern the maids' true thoughts... That's good as well. She always shares those tidbits with me. If not for her, I wouldn't have learned about the dark sides of many people who usually appear normal and kind... Audrey poured the potion into a bowl and placed it on the floor. She watched Susie approach and begin lapping up the potion, unable to curb the anticipation in her heart. Susie might be influenced by the potion and become unstable. But it's alright. Psychiatrist Miss Audrey is already prepared to use Placate at any moment! Yes, I prefer the name Psychoanalysis. That sounds more professional. Audrey stared intently at Susie with her beautiful emerald-like eyes and saw the golden retriever's pupils gradually fade and become vertical. Dark gold scales seemed to grow beneath her thick fur, and Susie's spirituality radiated outward as though interweaving with the space throughout the villa. After calming her nervous emotions, Audrey scrutinized Susie's condition. If anything abnormal happened to Susie, she would immediately use the Beyonder power Psychoanalysis. Suddenly, Susie's voice sounded in her ears. "Audrey, I'm done!" Audrey was momentarily at a loss for words. In her dream, Daisy returned to East Borough and to the old apartment she had lived in for years. She pushed open the door and saw her mother, Liz, and her sister, Freja, doing the laundry diligently. Daisy instantly became delighted and was just about to join them. She was in charge of ironing the laundry. At this moment, she heard knocking at the door. She turned her head and realized that the visitor was a young man in a black-and-white checkered police uniform. The officer had black hair and green eyes, with a somewhat blurry face. He held a notebook and fountain pen as he asked, "In the Capim case, apart from what you mentioned, is there anything else you didn't mention to us?" "Nothing important," Daisy answered groggily. The handsome officer looked down at his notebook and said, "It's fine. I'm willing to listen." Daisy looked back at the clothes hanging to dry, feeling as though she had forgotten some instructions. She honestly described all sorts of trivialities. In the end, she said, "...After I was abducted, my mother and sister had hired a private detective to search for me. His name is Mr. Sherlock Moriarty. He's a good man. Although he didn't find me directly, he later contacted a reporter to help me get compensated with the foundation money..." The black-haired and green-eyed officer looked up again and glanced at Daisy before revealing a warm smile. "Very good. Your answer is very satisfactory. "Do you still remember the private detective's appearance?" Daisy nodded. Without any alarm, she saw Mr. Sherlock Moriarty standing beside her. The detective had a thick beard and wore gold-rimmed glasses. He looked almost identical to the man in her memories. After the black-haired, green-eyed officer sized up the image several times, he vanished without Daisy noticing. For some reason, her mother and sister had also disappeared. She ran through East Borough in search of the familiar figures, but eventually awoke from the sorrowful dream. Seeing the dark ceiling of her school dormitory, she lay there in a daze for several seconds. Daisy didn't make a sound as she turned her body and buried half her face into the pillow. At the edge of the pillow, a wet stain gradually spread. The person who had entered Daisy's dream was none other than Leonard Mitchell. Although his investigation into the similarities between the two cases was merely meant to give him time to deal with his own affairs, he hadn't neglected to make a perfunctory effort. In the end, he actually discovered a problem. The cases of Lanevus and Capim both involved a private detective named Sherlock Moriarty, as well as his friend, Reporter Mike Joseph... Although they had only appeared at the periphery of these matters, this is still a lead worth investigating. Heh, that Sherlock Moriarty looks somewhat familiar. Which fugitive is he? Leonard recalled what he had seen in the dream as he put on his red glove and entered the basement of Saint Samuel Cathedral. Just as he greeted the team captain, Soest, he saw a partner approach and hand him two thin sheets of paper. "The information regarding the red-eyed man from the Harvest Church is all here." "Thank you. Do you want to have lunch together?" Leonard asked with a smile. The Nighthawk shrugged and said, "No, as long as you stop making me have nightmares." "Deal." Leonard smiled as he received the dossier. He stood there without being in a hurry to sit down as he casually browsed through it. "Emlyn White. A vampire. Currently under the jurisdiction of the Church of Earth Mother... He once vanished for a period of time. His parents had hired private detectives to find him. Thanks to a particular Mr. Stuart, this matter was ultimately resolved by the famous detective, Sherlock Moriarty." Leonard's smile gradually froze as his expression turned serious. Sherlock Moriarty? He repeated the name in his mind. Klein wasn't in a rush to find an opportunity to engage in true acting. He toured Oravi Island's port city with the mindset of a tourist, finding a brief and rare moment of relaxation in his tense life. The city was populated mostly by immigrants from Loen. Its cuisine wasn't much different from that of the kingdom's east coast, except for the rare fruits and varied seafood that gave it a distinctive character. Oravi was rich in natural resources and occupied a key position along the safe sea routes. The standard of living was fairly high. Even farmers in the suburbs could save money from their orchards. This didn't mean Oravi had no poor or lower-class residents. That class consisted mainly of former slaves, as Loen's parliament had abolished slavery long ago. After eating a sweet, juicy fruit, Klein watched the sky darken. He rounded a street corner and entered a bar named Sweet Lemon. It was a famous gathering place for adventurers in Oravi. Klein planned to buy the two remaining supplementary ingredients for the Marionettist potion--the relatively common drago tree bark and Sonia's Golden Spring water. The bar was quite lively. Many people raised their cups around the boxing ring and cheered loudly. At the surrounding tables, patrons who looked like adventurers discussed all kinds of rumors in hushed tones. Just as Klein was squeezing towards the bar counter, he suddenly heard his name. "I'm Gehrman Sparrow. You should know who I am. I received a treasure map and need to hire some helpers. It's not because I'm afraid, but because I can't carry that much treasure alone..." In a corner, a green-eyed man in his thirties held a half-full glass of liquor and spoke to two men and two women whose status as merchants or adventurers was unclear. You're also named Gehrman Sparrow? A treasure map... Why does that sound like a scam... News of my killing Wormtongue has already reached this place from Bayam? Yes, it was likely carried by telegrams or travelers. Therefore, many people know my name and deeds but not what I look like... Swindlers are taking advantage of this to impersonate me and defraud others... Klein moved closer as realization dawned on him. The green-eyed man drank a mouthful of liquor and slammed the glass onto the table. "I don't mind whether you refuse or agree, but I hate it when people make me wait! "Do you wish to be like Wormtongue?" The young man opposite him said, somewhat intimidated, "I know you're a powerful adventurer..." "So?" The green-eyed man cut off the man's words. At that moment, his collar tightened. Someone lifted him off his feet and threw him out the door. Klein didn't provide an explanation as he directly threw the man out of the door with a stoic expression. Then, he drew his revolver and aimed it at the spot where the man had fallen to the ground. He pulled the trigger without any hesitation. Bang! As the green-eyed man hit the ground, he saw a spark flare near his crotch. Terrified, he swallowed his curses and scrambled away. Without need for an explanation, his cowardly reaction proved that he wasn't Gehrman Sparrow. Klein ignored the intended victims, who stood there in a daze. He politely blew across the muzzle of his revolver before slipping it back into his shoulder holster. He then walked slowly to the bar through the ensuing silence.
Chapter 614: Adventurer Association Klein sat in front of the bar counter and slammed his fist onto the counter. "One glass of Southville beer." Behind him, a few bouncers hesitated about whether to come over to give him a warning or pretend that no one had fired a shot. The bartender signaled the bouncers with a glance as he picked up a glass and chuckled. "Why don't you try a cup of Sweet Lemon? "Our boss once went to Trier to learn mixology. He has mastered many of the cocktail recipes left behind by Emperor Roselle, and he personally created Oravi's most popular drink, Sweet Lemon." Klein wasn't moved as he calmly replied, "I only drink beer." "Alright." The bartender made no rush to fetch a bottle of Southville beer. Smiling, he asked, "Sir, are you an adventurer?" Klein nodded without answering. The bartender continued without hesitation, smiling as he said, "Perhaps you should meet our boss. He's very friendly to new adventurers and is willing to treat them to drinks. Besides, he can offer you some assistance." Klein, who had come with the intention of purchasing the supplementary ingredients of a Marionettist, didn't reject the offer. He took out a brass penny and flicked it before catching it firmly. He placed the penny on the bar as a tip to thank the bartender for the information, then slowly stood and followed a bouncer to the second floor, entering a room at the far end of the corridor. The room was covered with thick, brownish-yellow, soft carpet. There was a faint smell of high-quality coal burning, mixed with the aroma of a cigar. A middle-aged man with blond hair combed neatly back reclined in a chair, puffing on a cigar as he read the newspapers. Six bodyguards surrounded him. Although Klein wasn't a Beyonder of the Spectator domain and couldn't determine the bodyguards' particular traits or strength, nor did he belong to the Mystery Pryer or Monster pathway and see secrets others couldn't discover, his spiritual intuition told him that they were definitely Beyonders--Beyonders who posed some degree of threat to him. The middle-aged man put down the newspaper and tugged at the collar of his black shirt before slowly standing. He extended his right hand and said, "Welcome to Oravi, my adventurer friend." His blue eyes had a smile to them as he looked rather sincere. Klein extended his right hand and shook his without a word, waiting for the man to speak. The middle-aged man pointed to a sofa opposite the reclining chair and chuckled. "I'm the boss here, Bilt Brando. "I was once an adventurer of considerable strength. I've survived to this day and earned quite a bit." He's very confident in his strength, daring to state it so openly... Klein didn't stand on ceremony as he sat down. He leaned slightly forward and waited expressionlessly for Bilt to speak. Receiving no response from the adventurer, Bilt sat again and drew on his cigar before saying leisurely, "To be honest, I have an ulterior motive for meeting every new adventurer." He pointed to the sea chart on the desk and said in a resonant voice, "East of the Rorsted Archipelago, the seas grow increasingly chaotic. The military and the Church have less and less power, until they can protect little beyond their own harbors. "The sea around here is a pirate playground, extremely disadvantageous to us adventurers. Therefore, I wish to organize everyone to form a loosely connected alliance, so that we can band together when faced with danger. "This alliance has no strictly binding terms. You can choose to turn a blind eye when other adventurers encounter danger, and no one will punish you. However, if you encounter a similar situation, don't expect anyone to help you. "In addition, I can promise this: members of the alliance will receive my lowest prices when buying from me, and at least the market price when selling their spoils." After finishing the description, Bilt smiled at the new adventurer. He chuckled and asked, "What do you think of it? Are you interested in joining this loose alliance? Don't worry. You won't need to make any additional payment. Our purpose is only to render assistance when faced with pirates." Klein nodded. "It sounds pretty good." "Haha, I think so too. I once considered naming this association the Adventuring Brotherhood, but I felt that 'brotherhood' was too restrictive, so I changed it to the Adventurer Association," Bilt said self-deprecatingly. Having said that, he lowered his hand with the cigar and smacked his lips. He shook his head and smiled. "Sorry, I forgot to ask your name." Klein maintained his posture and replied in a deep voice, "Gehrman Sparrow." "Gehrman Sparrow..." Bilt's eyelids jumped as his smile instantly stiffened. The guards around him clearly tensed up as though they were facing a formidable enemy. Bilt quickly composed himself. Without trying to verify whether this was the real Gehrman Sparrow or merely an impostor, he chuckled and said, "Is there anything you wish to buy? I have quite a lot of good stuff here." "Sonia's Golden Spring water," Klein said with a calm expression while inwardly feeling cautious. He didn't mention the drago tree bark since there was a high chance of buying the ingredient at herb stores. Bilt Brando heaved a sigh of relief and smiled. "Easy. "30 pounds for 100 ml. "Trust me. Even if you head to Sonia Island, it will only be a few pounds cheaper than this price. Those barbarians from Feysac have sealed off the fountain's source, so it's difficult for others to get any of it." "Deal." Klein had a rough idea of the price of the Golden Spring water, and he knew that 30 pounds for 100 ml was indeed rather cheap. After completing the deal, Bilt was just about to speak after some deliberation when he suddenly heard knocking. After receiving his permission, a bouncer entered and leaned over, whispering into his ear. Bilt's expression instantly sank as his entire person appeared abnormally cold. He suffused an indescribable killing intent. Indeed, he possesses impressive strength. If he wasn't a famous adventurer in the past, he must've been a famous pirate... He should be a Mid-Sequence Beyonder... Klein calmly assessed him. Bilt turned his head and said to Klein with some difficulty, "Mr. Sparrow, I have matters to tend to. "We can have drinks together if the opportunity arises." "Okay." Klein slowly got up, without any intention of involving himself in Bilt's matters. Of course, this didn't mean that he wasn't curious, but curiosity was never something that could change the way he did things. After leaving Sweet Lemon, Klein successfully returned to his inn. City of Silver, during the "daytime" marked by frequent lightning. After Derrick Berg finished practicing the various Beyonder powers of a Solar High Priest, he followed the edge of the training field toward the twin towers. After numerous Tarot Gatherings, he had gradually discerned a pattern and could roughly judge, from the frequency of the alternating lightning, when Mr. Fool would pull him above the gray fog. And now was the final "day." Because of this, he had to visit the library and read historical records concerning the ancient gods so that he could offer the information to Mr. Fool. After passing through the partitioned area of the training field, Derrick subconsciously looked inside and saw exploration members resting inside. It was the exploration team led by the six-member council's chief, Colin Iliad! They had recently finished the exploration based on the information they had received from Jack, and they had returned to the City of Silver where they were now in quarantine. With a somewhat heavy heart, Derrick withdrew his gaze and continued to the steeple's third-floor library. He was about to walk toward the bookshelf holding all the ancient books of legends when he caught sight of a familiar figure from the corner of his eye. It was a fair and beautiful woman in her thirties. She wore a long black robe embroidered with mysterious purple patterns. Her curly silvery-gray hair cascaded down. She was none other than Lovia Tiffany, the elder of the six-member council who had been imprisoned for a prolonged period! She swept her pale gray eyes over him, and Derrick felt as though his soul had been pierced. He involuntarily stiffened for a second. "Greetings, Elder Lovia." He hurriedly lowered his head as he pressed his hand to his chest. Lovia walked over and nodded gently. "I've been removed from quarantine." After making this calm declaration, she turned and left. Derrick stood rooted to the spot as cold sweat seeped from his back. Why has she been released? Has the six-member council already determined that she's fine? Derrick wondered as his nerves grew unusually taut. Monday afternoon, above the gray fog. Klein rested his elbows on the armrests and interlaced his fingers, watching beams of crimson light flare before receding into blurry figures. Then, he heard Miss Justice's brisk greeting. "Good afternoon, Mr. Fool~"
Chapter 615: Grayish-white Fog While Miss Justice exchanged greetings with everyone, The Hermit Cattleya remained silent and observed as before. She didn't involve herself, as though she were an outsider at the gathering. She watched as Miss Justice and Miss Magician conjured their Roselle diary pages to pay off their previous debts. Then, she carefully glanced at Mr. Fool without daring to look straight at him. Yet, she still wasn't able to see further through the special gray fog. Her dark purple eyes were only capable of seeing clothes that were definitely conjured. With three pages of Roselle's diary in hand, Klein wasn't as eager to read them as before. After all, he had already handled and used a Grade 0 Sealed Artifact and knew what the Uniqueness of a Beyonder pathway looked like. He had even intimidated such a divine artifact, so he believed that nothing Emperor Roselle had written could greatly shock him. Unless he was given a Demoness Blessing by some powerhouse with a unique ability and temporarily became a woman... Klein joked inwardly as he surveyed the long bronze table in interest. Eh, Ma'am Hermit's curiosity differs from that of Miss Justice and the others. She pays close attention to Roselle's diary? Klein withdrew his gaze and noted this discovery. Then, he casually read the yellowish-brown goatskin. "22nd April. We plan to enter and explore the Abyss." "23rd April. We sailed across the pitch-black ocean, passed through the liquid-like fog, and arrived at a mountain peak resembling a monster. Behind it lay endless black fog that seemed to blanket an entire continent. "However, looking down from the peak, the abyss appeared endless and boundless. I joked with Edwards that if I committed suicide by jumping off that cliff, I might never reach the ground and would remain in a state of perpetual free fall." Upon reading this, Klein nearly raised his eyebrows. He couldn't believe that Roselle would dare organize his knights and sailors to explore the region's periphery after seeing the Abyss. Isn't he afraid of dying? Legend has it that it's a place capable of corrupting everything and causing all life to perish! At this stage, Roselle definitely hadn't reached Sequence 4 and wasn't a demigod. He was at best Sequence 5, or even lower... If it were me, I definitely would've turned the ship around and reported it to the Church... At that moment, Klein gained a profound understanding of the vast difference between Roselle and himself. In addition, Roselle's description of the Abyss's periphery reminded Klein of the mysterious stone doors in Amon's mausoleum. A similar scene had appeared after the puppet of Horamick, an archbishop of the Church of Steam and Machinery, touched them. I wonder what Roselle discovered there... At the very least, he didn't die from his exploration. He still had an exciting life after that... Klein moved his gaze down and read the remaining content on the diary page. "24th April. We proceeded down the peak in an attempt to probe deeper. "The thick black fog is bitterly cold, as though it can corrode both flesh and soul. Haha, fortunately, the Dark King carries certain items that resist this corruption. Otherwise, I suspect my Knights of the Apocalypse and I would join Farron's Undead Legion. "It's very quiet, and we didn't discover anything." "25th April. We saw devils, but they were in the form of rotting corpses. "Behind the black, jagged mountain, down a slush-filled opening that could hardly be called a path, we found all kinds of devil corpses in both ordinary and unimaginable places. "It was as though they had all been killed at the same moment." "26th April. There is nothing but corpses and silence, with no end in sight. "The items aboard the Dark King have begun to show signs of corruption. "I've seldom had fear over the past few years, but here, that fear of the unknown is like an invisible hand that clasps my heart tightly. "I have to leave! I have to return! I can't stay here any longer!" What happened after this? Did Emperor Roselle successfully escape the Abyss's periphery, or did he encounter something else? What did the abnormality there signify? An intense battle? Klein felt a trace of anticipation as he turned to the second page, only to be disappointed that it wasn't connected. "8th May. My beloved Bernadette is almost two. The older she grows, the more lovable she becomes. She's truly a young lady who lives up to the excellent genes of her mother and me. "Hearing her clearly call me daddy and seeing her bubbly figure, I suddenly felt a sense of satisfaction. "Ever since I transmigrated to this world, I've done many things. Some were hardly honorable, but I've felt no shame over them, nor have I ever regretted them. On the one hand, this is because I find it very difficult to curb my desires, making me susceptible to the influence of my environment. Heh heh, I have to thank fate that I've never met a Desire Apostle of the Devil pathway. According to the records, I would definitely succumb to a Beyonder of that Sequence. I might even be killed instantly. "On the other hand, I still feel alienated from this world. My parents here are very kind to me, and I've worked hard to make them proud, but I know my feelings for them aren't genuine. I feel the same way about Matilda. It's more possessive instinct than love. "I have to admit that my mental state resembles playing a role-playing game in virtual reality. My parents, siblings, and friends are all non-player characters. I can devote some emotion to them, but never anything deep. Therefore, I can join all kinds of depraved gatherings without guilt. I can treat people I know well with cold ruthlessness. It's just like when I played The Elder Scrolls. I could slaughter an entire village over a chicken. "But after Bernadette was born, I realized that I had an additional sense of belonging to this world. I was no longer as estranged from it. "This is my child, a living child of mine. "Perhaps this is what so-called maturity is?" Without children, it's impossible to understand this feeling. No, I don't even have a girlfriend... However, I have to remain vigilant against the state of mind mentioned in this entry... It might not have existed in the past, but that doesn't mean it won't appear in the future. The higher the Sequence, the more one's godhood outweighs one's humanity... Klein sighed silently as he turned to the third diary page. "6th January, a brand new year, a brand new beginning. "After advancing to Artisan, I finally have the power to do that! "That is to create the mysterious silver plate in my memories. There is a high chance that my transmigration was a result of it! "In fact, after I became a Savant, I could already recall its appearance, as well as the strange symbols and patterns on its surface. But the past me could clearly sense that I wasn't able to replicate something like that." "9th January. I finally succeeded after repeated failures. "Holding the silver plate covered in special symbols and patterns, I tried my best to inject it with spirituality and activate it. "An endless grayish-white fog seemed to surface before my eyes, but nothing happened. "Is it a problem with the material, or am I lacking certain requisites?" "10th January. Drawing on my memories of transmigration, I recreated my state at the time and believed nothing was missing. However, the mysterious silver plate only showed me the strange gray fog. It couldn't help me accomplish anything. "Since this doesn't work, how did I succeed in my transmigration back then? "I temporarily abandoned my attempts and destroyed the silver plate I had created. Perhaps when I become a High-Sequence Beyonder and a demigod, I'll be able to interpret those patterns and symbols and uncover the truth behind my transmigration. "Yes, I'll definitely become a demigod! I'm the protagonist of this era!" Grayish-white fog? The Emperor saw an endless grayish-white fog after replicating the mysterious silver plate from Earth! Klein's eyes suddenly shrank when he read the diary entry. There happened to be an unchanging, endless gray fog beneath his feet! Could our transmigrations be connected to this mysterious space? But why couldn't the Emperor enter when I can? According to the diary entries from the final stages of his life, he definitely never unraveled the mystery of the silver plate. Otherwise, he would've thought of this place in his moment of utter despair and madness. He would've used it as a final recourse... Klein raised his head and looked beyond the ancient palace. He recalled that deep in this mysterious space, there was a staircase of light that seemed to lead to heaven. It seemed to correspond to his Sequence. The staircase appeared to have been built for giants, and its destination was the gray fog, which seemed to support something suspended in midair. Does the secret of our transmigration lie there? Klein made the diary pages in his hand vanish, leaned back in his chair, and said evenly, "You may begin." Derrick had originally planned to request the Sequence 6 potion formula that followed Solar High Priest, but Elder Lovia's release made him temporarily abandon the idea. He couldn't wait to report everything that had happened and obtain the necessary guidance. Considering how this was still the transaction segment, he held back his desire as he waited in silence. There's something on Little Sun's mind... Did something unexpected happen in the City of Silver? Audrey thoughtfully withdrew her gaze and likewise made no purchase request. At that moment, Alger surveyed the group and spoke. "I need the potion formula of Ocean Songster." Indeed, he's already a Sequence 6, a Wind-blessed... Isn't he a member of the Church of Storms? Why is he looking elsewhere for the Ocean Songster potion formula? Obtaining it internally from the Church would be much easier... Does he have secrets he wishes to keep from the Church of Storms, or is he merely pretending to belong to it? Numerous theories instantly occurred to Cattleya, and she quietly took note. "I can keep an eye out for it." Upon noticing The Hermit's response, Alger asked, "Ma'am, is there anything you need? "I can search for clues ahead of time, so as to trade for the potion formula." 1. Author's Note: A meme involving Dark Souls II. Farron's Undead Legion, also known as the Abyss Watchers, who were corrupted by the Abyss.
Chapter 616: Silver Lining What do I need? Cattleya silently chuckled, having sensed that The Hanged Man was probing her with a very ordinary question. Any need would reveal clues! Never mind that I've already obtained the Sequence 4 Mysticologist potion formula for the Mystery Pryer pathway and am accumulating contribution points for one of the main ingredients. Even without those, I have no shortage of relevant channels--and far more than one... Recalling the Sea God Scepter Mr. Fool wielded, Cattleya had another thought. She smiled and said, "I need a demigod-level mystical item with acceptable side effects." At that instant, Alger nearly retorted, asking her not to crack a joke. Even in the Church of Storms, one might go years without obtaining such an item, much less a Beyonder who was clearly only at the Mid-Sequence level! If I had an item at the demigod level without any real negative side effects, why wouldn't I keep it for my own use? Alger knew that The Hermit was using mockery to respond to his attempt at sounding her out, but he wasn't as irascible as his peers. He slowly took a deep breath and said, "I'll keep an eye out. "But Ma'am, you should know very well that just an effective clue towards such an item might be enough to cover the cost of an Ocean Songster's potion formula." ...Very composed. Not easily angered. That's quite unlike the usual style of the Church of Storms... Was my first conclusion wrong? Is he merely posing as a priest of Storms? No, I can't assume that. He might simply not dare lose his temper under Mr. Fool's gaze. Or perhaps he's just an exception within the Church of Storms. There might not be many, but they can't be exceptionally rare... Cattleya wasn't greedy. Rather than test him again, she nodded. "I know." As their conversation ended, no one else made a request during the transaction segment. Several members already had the means to obtain what they needed, so there was no need to request a purchase. Audrey and Fors were mainly waiting for their subsequent potion formulas. Others were unable to spend in advance because of their finances or circumstances. This included Emlyn, who yearned for the Sanguine's Viscount inheritance, and Miss Magician, who wanted a mystical item. Indeed, as everyone gradually sheds their status as Low-Sequence Beyonders, advancement is no longer so rapid. The frequency of transactions will also decline sharply. In the past, there were basically one or two deals every week, but now there might be only one every two or three weeks. In the future, there might not be one for three or four months... Unsure whether this was good or bad, Klein nodded gently to indicate that it was time for the free exchange. Audrey looked at Derrick and waited for him to describe the unexpected situation at the City of Silver. Derrick didn't let her "expectations" down. Before anyone could speak, he earnestly said, "Elder Lovia has been released. I encountered her at the library." Shepherd Lovia has been released? The entire team she led was corrupted in body and soul by the True Creator, so how could there be nothing wrong with her? What is the six-member council thinking? Klein originally wanted to think something along the lines of, If there's nothing wrong with Lovia, I'll chop off my head and give it to the True Creator to kick around like a ball. However, considering that oaths and curses involving deities might lead to terrible consequences, he rationally changed his train of thought. Of course, I don't have to be that careful with me above the gray fog... He sighed inwardly. "Elder Lovia has been released? That Shepherd?" Audrey quickly recalled what the name meant. Back then, Little Sun had used his possession by Blasphemer Amon and Mr. Fool's help to expose the fact that the entire exploration team had been corrupted by the True Creator. That team had been led by Lovia, whose Sequence, Shepherd, belonged to the True Creator's Secrets Suppliant pathway! "Yes." Derrick nodded earnestly as he looked towards The Hanged Man. Alger thought for a moment before asking, "Has your Chief returned to the City of Silver?" Why would Mr. Hanged Man suddenly ask about this... Ah, right. To release such an important figure, it's impossible that the other elders of the six-member council wouldn't wait for the Chief's return... If the Chief hadn't returned and they made this decision without his consent, the situation was even more terrible than anyone imagined--so terrible that they couldn't even wait for him... If the Chief had returned, however, Lovia's release was probably connected to the outcome of the expedition. According to Little Sun, it was the City of Silver's only recent expedition. Sigh, why didn't I think of this? Audrey, you're still lacking in experience... Audrey reflected and consoled herself in thought. "Yes, not long ago." Derrick was astonished by Mr. Hanged Man's accurate deduction. At this moment, Fors, who had been listening quietly, combined what she knew from before and suddenly had an idea. "Mr. Sun, could this be the situation? "Your Chief led the exploration team and that little boy, Jack, to seek a path to the outside world, but they discovered that the True Creator's power was required. Heh heh, this isn't a lie I'm fabricating, but an inference based on the facts. That boy Jack's father belonged to the Aurora Order, and they were seeking the True Creator's holy residence before arriving where you are. "Therefore, for the entire City of Silver, your Chief decided to release Shepherd Lovia after returning." "If that's really the case, Mr. Sun would be in grave danger," Audrey said worriedly. Fors's words made Derrick's heart sink. At this moment, Alger shook his head. "No, I have the exact opposite belief. "Miss Magician's inference is identical to my theory, but I believe this will make it safer for The Sun!" "Why?" Derrick's heart calmed down as he asked. Isn't that simple? Balance! Klein scoffed inwardly. "Any sentient creature with eyes and a brain can recognize the danger posed by the True Creator. Your Chief definitely won't place all his bets on 'Him.' He needs a force capable of counterbalancing the True Creator. "As for you, the one who exposed their ploy, you were possessed by Blasphemer Amon, so you might represent another possibility.
