He knew that the number of believers in Earth Mother had indeed increased significantly. In the past, it would've been a miracle for even a handful of people to attend daytime prayers on weekdays. Now, there were often nearly ten. Father Utravsky looked down at the busy vampire priest and chuckled. "Anyone can tell if they aren't blind. "You have contributed greatly to this. Without the medicine you prepared, your treatment of those affected by the plague, and your sincere willingness to teach people about medicine, our faith wouldn't have been so readily accepted by this borough's residents. Emlyn held a cloth and straightened his back. He tipped his chin slightly. "I was only acting." What, what do you mean by "our faith?" Don't lump me with you! Emlyn's expression twisted before he said with a smile, "Speaking of the blind, it reminds me of a joke. It's said that the demand for blind people in Backlund far exceeds supply. This is because they are widely believed to be most suitable to be jurors." Father Utravsky ignored the joke and said benevolently, "Regardless of your goal, you have contributed greatly to spreading faith in Earth Mother. "Besides, this also proves that you have a kind heart." Peh! I said so back then, but why didn't you believe me? Emlyn looked up at the priest's massive body before retracting his gaze in silence. After finishing his work at the cathedral, he changed into his usual clothes and put on a silk top hat to shelter himself from the sun. He then stepped onto Rose Street. He discreetly surveyed his surroundings and didn't notice any signs of monitoring. That Red Glove named Leonard really hasn't appeared again... I thought exposing his secret and buying Tinder would result in my being constantly investigated... Emlyn White shook his head almost imperceptibly, feeling puzzled. At first, he had planned to adopt The Hanged Man's suggestion and draw the Red Gloves' attention, thereby disrupting the surveillance of the Sanguine's upper echelons. He could then achieve a perfect balance by relying on Utravsky, the Church of Earth Mother's Blessed. But things didn't develop as he had expected. Leonard Mitchell had apparently left Backlund very quickly. At the end of February, Emlyn had made a detour to 7 Pinster Street while he was out once, only to discover that it was uninhabited. Without thinking about this matter any further, he walked to the end of the street, got onto a rental carriage and headed straight for the Odora villa. An attendant led him to a study on the first floor, where he saw many Sanguine who had recently come of age. Among them was one who had already become a Baron. I'm not the only one? he thought as he closed the door. He then asked the host, Cosmi Odora, "My lord, wasn't I called here because Lord Nibbs summoned me?" He had said "my lord" rather indifferently, as though addressing Cosmi by name. This was because he was also a Sanguine Baron, the difference being that he hadn't publicized it. Cosmi was a very refined middle-aged gentleman. He smiled and said, "All of you are outstanding young Sanguine. My grandfather has entrusted all of you with some tests." Another Sanguine Baron, Rus Bathory, who had been lucky enough to receive an inheritance, asked, "What kind of tests?" Cosmi took a sip of dark-red blood blended with grape wine as his gaze swept the room. "You might not know this, but the Snake of Fate from the Life School of Thought disappeared quite some time ago." As Emlyn White and the other Sanguine looked puzzled, Cosmi continued, "But I believe all of you know that the Life School of Thought is a loose coalition held together by a shared belief in fate. It formed under the immense pressure exerted by the seven orthodox Churches at the beginning of the Fifth Epoch and consists of Beyonders who consider themselves absolutely rational and aloof, those who worship the Primordial Moon, and those who seek the essence of life and spirituality. "Thanks to the Snake of Fate, there hadn't been many serious internal problems. Their worship of the Primordial Moon was ultimately restricted to a fixed symbolic meaning. Furthermore, formula exchanges were integrated with a master-apprentice system of inheritance. "Unfortunately, heh, with the disappearance of the Snake of Fate, this process has been disrupted. The Primordial Moon's believers rapidly grew fanatical, producing a fracture in the faction that represents fate. An intense conflict ensued as a result. "This situation was exploited by the Rose School of Thought. It dealt them considerable damage." Emlyn White, Rus Bathory, and the other Sanguine remained perplexed. Having provided the background, Cosmi turned to the details. "Worshipers of the Primordial Moon are our eternal enemies. They have always been hunting us, concocting us into potions to gain power! "Now, we will not let go of such an opportunity. "Here is a list of Primordial Moon worshipers and information about their circumstances. Whoever finds and kills them will win this test. My grandfather and several other important figures will reward you generously. "If you complete only part of the list, the result will be decided by the number eliminated. "Of course, these people were specifically selected because all of you are capable of dealing with them. The important figures will track down the rest." Upon hearing the first few sentences, Emlyn White had no intention of participating despite his hatred for those "artificial" vampires. He found the matter troublesome, laborious, and tiresome. He would rather stay home and quietly chat with his dolls. Once he realized it was a competition and noticed the gazes Rus Bathory and the other Sanguine directed at him, Emlyn abruptly straightened his back and raised his chin. "No problem." His red eyes slowly swept across the other creatures in the room. On the Future, inside a spacious room with an attached bathroom. Klein stood before the window, looking out at the undulating blue ocean. In a good mood, he breathed in the cold wind from the north. The flagship of the Admiral of Stars had already separated from the other ships in the fleet as it began to cruise alone. After an indeterminate period, two whaling ships appeared ahead. The moment their crews noticed the Future's flag with its stars and eye, they reacted nervously. They quickly adjusted their positions, turning their starboard sides toward the Future and readying their cannons to fire at any moment. At the same time, explosive-propelled spears and harpoons were trained in the same direction. The large, blond fishermen of the Gargas Archipelago gripped tridents and guns as they braced for an attack, some standing and others crouching. Klein also noticed that there were a number of women with Hulk-like physiques. It was obvious at a glance that they were sturdy and formidable in a fight. The Future paid no heed to their "welcome." It continued sailing past them, heading deeper along the whaling route. After sailing for a while, Klein saw more pirate ships ahead. They were clustered around the periphery of the sea route, their motives unclear. The Future approached without ceremony. The pirate ships immediately scattered like startled birds. Sensing the Future slow down, Klein left his room to investigate. Just as he approached the captain's cabin, he discovered Cattleya walking out. This woman wore a thick pair of glasses on her nose bridge, hiding her mysterious purple eyes. She glanced at Klein and said succinctly, "Someone discovered ruins said to date from the Fourth Epoch on the seabed in these waters. "We plan to take a look on our way." The seabed? Fourth Epoch ruins? Klein instantly recalled the rumor he had heard in the Lerdal Bar. So this piece of news has already spread? I was wondering why I got to learn it so easily... he thought with sudden understanding.
Chapter 640: Female Pirate Klein was curious about the outcome of the exploration. Without asking further, he passed the captain's cabin and descended the stairs. After a few seconds, he felt his throat itch. He couldn't help but raise his fist to his mouth and cough. Klein wasn't surprised by this inevitable development. He had carried the Biological Poison Bottle for more than two hours the previous night. Only late that night, after confirming that Admiral of Stars and her crew had no intention of attacking him, had he moved the mystical item into his black suitcase. Unfortunately, he had already fallen ill. Of course, he hadn't carried the Biological Poison Bottle for very long, and his body wasn't weakened, so the resulting illness wasn't serious. His tonsils were merely swollen and painful. Cattleya, who was walking slowly behind, saw this scene, but she didn't find it a problem. Instead, she found it normal. Every knowledgeable Beyonder knew that mystical items inevitably had negative effects. Following the example of the seven orthodox Churches, they classified items whose severe effects prevented prolonged possession or use as Sealed Artifacts. Cattleya had sold or exchanged many of her low- and mid-level mystical items, both to improve her chances of survival and because managing the negative effects of multiple items was troublesome. Avoiding one effect often meant suffering another, and some could even combine into something worse. Therefore, for most Beyonders, the disadvantages outweighed the advantages. She had discovered that Gehrman Sparrow was armed to the teeth with mystical items, Beyonder weapons, and spiritual charms. Even amid her astonishment, she had begun guessing what negative effects he faced. From what she saw today, one of them was a simple, temporary illness. With steady steps, Klein reached the deck and saw Frank Lee. He was still dressed in a white shirt and dungarees, his arms stained with dirt as though he didn't feel the cold wind sweeping across the deck. "Good morning, Gehrman." Frank waved warmly and said, "Here, try my latest product. This will definitely be the most popular item at sea!" As he spoke, he raised his other hand. In it was a broad, fat fish of an unknown species. No, I don't want to know what "monster" you have cooked up this time... Klein paused in his footsteps as he looked at him with a cold expression. Frank Lee noticed nothing amiss in his attitude. He drew a dagger from his waist, stabbed the fish, and sliced it open. Blood flowed out and landed squarely in a large beer mug on the deck. It gave off no fishy smell. "Smell that? What an intoxicating aroma of alcohol!" Frank Lee half-closed his eyes and said fervently, "This fish has red wine instead of blood. That means the wine contains plenty of nutrients!" Klein found himself at a loss for words. Frank looked excitedly at the surrounding sailors before saying to Gehrman Sparrow, "Do you know what the greatest difficulty at sea is? Running out of alcohol while nowhere near shore! As long as this kind of fish can reproduce rapidly and become common throughout the ocean, we'll never lack alcohol, no matter where we are. They can also be divided into species. Some will produce Lanti Proof; others, Nepos, red wine, or beer. Beer needs to come from sharks or whales, though. Otherwise, there won't be enough!" Isn't the greatest difficulty a lack of water? Of course, all of you can replace water with beer most of the time because it doesn't spoil easily... Those poor fish... Klein was considering how to respond to Frank when Cattleya came on deck. She walked past him and questioned her first mate. "Is Nina done with her preparations?" "Yes, she has already finished off a bottle of Nepos!" Frank pointed toward a shadow cast by the sails. So the so-called preparations consist of drinking a bottle of Nepos, a Feysac specialty? The high-proof Nepos that can be set alight? Klein suddenly felt that Nina, the lady mentioned by the first mate, likely had Feysac blood. "Captain, I want a bottle of Sonia blood wine more!" In the dark, a female figure slowly stood up and walked over. She was more than 1.8 meters tall, with her blond hair casually tied in a high ponytail. Her features were rather plain, but she bore the distinctive traits of a Feysacian. Her skin was fair, and her eyes were dull. This lady named Nina wore a tight black suit made of fish skin. The top and bottom seemed to be a one-piece, fully accentuating her stunning figure. The outfit was already quite revealing, and Nina's breasts were far larger than average. It was obvious what the surrounding pirates were looking at. Klein felt a little embarrassed and wanted to look away. On second thought, however, Gehrman Sparrow was definitely not so inexperienced. All he could do was make his gaze vacant and look directly at Nina's face. "Gehrman, this is our boatswain, Nina! She's also the navigator's assistant. Haha, her Sequence is called Seafarer!" Frank Lee still held nothing back in his introductions. Apart from his research into crossbreeding, this Poison Expert is rather simple... I remember now that this lady named Nina has a bounty of 3,600 pounds. Her nickname is Seabed Murderer. Sigh, after seeing so many bounty notices, there are some I can't immediately recall... Klein looked Nina in the eyes and nodded calmly. "Good morning, Ma'am." Nina held back her smile and sized up Klein. "Good morning, Mr. Sparrow. "I'm very curious if Vice Admiral Ailment is really as charming as the rumors say?" As a female pirate who had spent years among the lower and middle classes, she was frank and direct with men and women alike, without the slightest coyness. She had originally intended to ask Gehrman Sparrow whether she lacked charm or whether his cold temperament explained why he had ignored her without the slightest reaction. However, the man before her was powerful: an adventurer who had nearly succeeded in hunting Vice Admiral Ailment and a lunatic who might draw his gun and fire at any moment. She wisely swallowed the teasing words and asked about Vice Admiral Ailment instead. ...How am I supposed to answer that? Klein said gloomily, "Her bounty is extremely charming." Nina was taken aback and at a loss for a response. Hence, she turned to look at Admiral of Stars. "Captain, do we begin now?" For some inexplicable reason, Cattleya suddenly recalled her own bounty. She nodded. "Begin." As soon as she said that, Nina strode to the side of the ship. Bracing herself with her right hand, she leaped into the sea and swam downward like a gigantic black fish. Several splashes followed as a few sailors jumped down to assist her. This... She dives the moment it's mentioned. She didn't need any additional time to prepare... This lady has the temperament of the Church of Storms. As expected of a Beyonder from the Sailor pathway... Klein looked over the side of the ship and couldn't help coughing. "You're sick?" Frank Lee asked directly. Klein nodded slightly and said, "A little." Frank thought for a moment, then rushed back into the cabin without a word or any explanation of where he was going. Beside him, Cattleya pushed up her heavy glasses and smiled. "Frank is a Poison Expert, but he's also an outstanding doctor." As expected of someone from the Planter pathway... Klein didn't ask further as he stood there, awaiting Nina's preliminary exploration. As the sudden silence grew awkward, Cattleya took a few steps forward and said, seemingly in passing, "In another day, we'll leave the whaling route." "But aren't we at least a week away from those waters?" Klein asked after a moment's thought. "That would be true if we followed the whaling route, but it would take us farther north on a long detour. I know a secret route that will let us reach the waters you seek in two or three days." Cattleya looked into Klein's eyes through her thick glasses, as though trying to determine how much he knew about those extremely dangerous waters. Klein considered this and simply said, "Very good. That's exactly what I want. "In addition, those waters are more illusory than real." Cattleya retracted her gaze in thought as she looked at the entrance to the cabin. Frank Lee ran over and held a green apple in his hand. "This is the outcome of another one of my projects. It's a crossbreed of medicine and fruit. It makes taking medicine more enjoyable!" He beamed as he handed Klein the apple. I'm afraid I'll end up even sicker after eating it... Klein glanced at Admiral of Stars and saw her nod gently. Only then did he force himself to accept the apple, remaining outwardly calm. He then bit into it. It had the taste of an ordinary apple. It just had a lot more juice, and its flesh was softer. After a few bites, Klein discovered that his throat had abruptly stopped hurting. He hadn't even noticed when his coughing had ceased. I have to admit that it's rather magical... As long as it doesn't involve animals or humans, Frank Lee is truly a genius who should be taken seriously by the Church of Earth Mother. Unfortunately, he ultimately became a devil-like figure... Klein looked at the Poison Expert and said frankly, "It's healed." "Very good." Frank didn't praise himself as he began casually introducing the pirates on the deck. After a while, Nina and the sailors assisting her swam to the surface and returned to the ship. She held a piece of metal corroded beyond recognition and a piece of black, hardened mud riddled with honeycomb-like holes. She grumbled to Cattleya, "Captain, there's no deep-sea well! "That well's mouth isn't even bigger than my breasts! "Of course, it's very deep and dark. It's unknown what's hidden in it." She gestured using her hands. "Exaggeration is a common trait of pirates and adventurers." Cattleya nodded without using the term "bragging." The mouth of the well is that narrow? Puzzled, Klein looked at the item in Nina's hand as he politely shifted his gaze away from the streams of water flowing down her body. Cattleya's gaze moved in sync with his as she said, "Go into the details."
Chapter 641: A Well Mouth That Humans Can't Pass Nina was a pirate who had risen through the ranks. She was often quick-tempered, but her wealth of experience made her dependable in a crisis. After some thought, she gave a serious account of what she had found. "The mouth of the well lies deep on the seabed. I needed time to adjust before I could acclimate to the temperature and pressure down there. That's why it took me so long to reach it. "It isn't easy to find, but the remains of the steel buildings are quite conspicuous. I spotted them once I'd acclimated. "They've completely collapsed or rusted away, so there's no telling what they originally looked like. Still, I could tell they once covered a vast area. They've merely shrunk a great deal since then." At this point, Nina chuckled and swept her gaze over all the men around her. A genuine female pirate really is different... Klein sighed inwardly. From his point of view, whether it was Admiral of Stars Cattleya, Vice Admiral Iceberg Edwina, or Vice Admiral Ailment Tracy, none of them could be considered a true female pirate. All of them hailed from major factions or secret organizations. When they were Low-Sequence Beyonders, they were either not at sea or were following important figures, so the work they did was relatively safe. Otherwise, they had been independent adventurers, never shaped by the character and atmosphere of low- and mid-level pirates. After Nina finished laughing, Cattleya pointed to the rusted item that could hardly be described as a metal beam. "This is part of one of the steel buildings?" "Yes, Captain. As you know, I don't know much about history or mysticism. All I could do was bring a piece back for you to inspect. You're the expert here." Nina smiled as she handed over the "metal beam." Then, she pointed at the black piece of hardened mud whose surface was riddled with holes. "Not far from the metal ruins, I found a well. It isn't very big. If anyone wants to call it 'huge,' I've certainly seen plenty of cannons more deserving of the word. "Those drunken adventurers are better at bragging than us pirates! "This is the mud from the inner layer of the well. I can't imagine how such patterns could be formed!" Nina repeatedly tapped the honeycombed dots on the black mud. Klein initially believed they were marks left by a dense volley of tiny projectiles, but after careful inspection, he suspected that the "patterns" were remnants of something that had rotted away. Each mark was very shallow, with edges that spread outward irregularly. Nina handed the black mud to Cattleya as she continued, "The well's mouth is really small. Even a child from Nas wouldn't be able to enter. "It's very deep. It even felt bottomless. In that environment, the interior was completely dark, as though something was slowly summoning me. Yes--slowly. "I found a few rocks nearby and threw them in, but there wasn't any response. In short, it's filled with water." Cattleya held up the "metal beam" and black mud, examining them closely through her thick glasses. "Since the opening is very small and humans can't enter it, there's no need for us to begin exploring immediately. It would be very dangerous. "Let's wait until I uncover the secrets hidden in these items and determine whether the ancient well is worth the risk before we return and make an attempt." "Aye aye, Captain!" Soaked through, Nina trembled in the cold wind. The way she shivered made all the surrounding pirates stare fixedly at her. Cattleya nudged her glasses and said to Nina, "You can drink a bottle of Sonia blood wine. There's no limit for the rest." "Long live the Captain!" Nina cried out in joy. An underwater well that humans can't enter... Klein, who had no desire to explore it, summarized Nina's description. Suddenly, he had a strange idea. Humans are unable to enter the well, but that doesn't mean that non-humans can't do it! Many deep-sea fish aren't necessarily that huge. There's a significant chance that they can pass through the well. As the "Sea God," he had the means to make marine creatures do his bidding by wielding the scepter! There's no rush. Let's see if Ma'am Hermit can learn anything from these two objects. I'll consider exploring it on the return trip; otherwise, I might draw the attention of some overwhelming danger... There still isn't enough information. There's no way to perform a divination... As his thoughts wandered, Klein's expression remained impassive. At that moment, Cattleya shot him a glance out of curiosity. Then, she retracted her gaze without betraying any sign of it. Why did she suddenly look at me? Was she watching what I was doing? It's impossible for her to know that I possess the Sea God Scepter and can make marine creatures do my bidding. That's not right. She does know, but she only knows that Mr. Fool wields Kalvetua's godhood scepter, not The World... Unless she has figured out that The World is The Fool... But that's even more impossible. Even Mr. Hanged Man still believes that The World is a Blessed. She hasn't even realized that... Looking at it from another angle, I'll consider it from the Admiral of Stars's perspective... She's pursued by knowledge and is a follower of Queen Mystic. She's loyal to the Moses Ascetic Order and has roamed the sea for years. She possesses plenty of knowledge and experience, so it wouldn't be strange for her to know that the Sea God domain includes the Beyonder power to control marine creatures. Therefore, after realizing that humans are unable to pass through the ancient well, she naturally connected it to the scepter in Mr. Fool's hand. Does she plan to request help in the future? Did she look at me to find out whether The World had also grasped the relevant information or had a similar idea? Countless ideas raced through Klein's mind. With the powers of Clown, he forcefully maintained his indifferent expression. He didn't react abnormally in any way. As Nina was about to draw the Sonia blood wine, Klein pressed down his hat and returned to the cabin. Just as he was about to approach the door, a figure suddenly surfaced in his mind. In a room on the cabin's upper level, the windows were tightly shut and the curtains drawn. A pair of blurry eyes was hidden behind them, silently watching the crowd on the deck as well as Gehrman Sparrow. Who is it? Klein didn't stop. He showed no hesitation as he entered the cabin normally as though nothing had happened. At three in the afternoon, the bright but not scorching sunlight shone into the garden adjacent to Stoen University. By the age of forty, Michele Deuth had already become a senior associate professor. Wearing a long tailcoat and a beautiful bow tie, he waited by the door. The previous evening, he had received a letter from an attendant of the Hall family, the wealthiest aristocratic family in East Chester County. It had been written on behalf of the daughter of an immensely influential Member of Parliament in the House of Lords. She was Miss Audrey Hall, reputed to be Backlund's most dazzling gem. This noble lady had mentioned in the letter that she had learned from a gathering that Mr. Michele Deuth was an outstanding collector and an aficionado of this domain. She very much wished to pay him a visit. Michele Deuth had no reason to refuse. Soon, a classic carriage with a family emblem arrived at the door. Two servants, who had been instructed to open the outer wrought-iron gates, guided the carriage around the garden to the front of the house. A housekeeper was the first to alight, followed by guards and maidservants. Next, a hand wearing a long white gauze glove was extended outside. With the help of the maidservants, Audrey elegantly stepped onto the carpet Michele had laid out. Michele was taken aback, and then his eyes lit up. He felt as though the flowers in the garden had instantly lost their color. He took two steps forward and took off his hat to bow. "Welcome, my honorable lady. "Your visit is an honor for me and my family." Audrey took off the veiled hat and passed it to her maidservant before exchanging a few pleasantries. Then, she followed Michele Deuth into the living room and entered the collector's room on the first floor. Here, Michele finally found his confidence as the master of the house. He began pointing at his collection and introducing the pieces from left to right. "This is a helmet from the White Rose War. After extensive research, it was determined that its owner was a member of the Sauron family. Back then, they were still royalty." The golden helmet had an intricate design. Birds and outspread wings adorned it, and the visor was formed from pieces of golden scales. "My ancestor obtained his first aristocratic title in that war," Audrey replied with keen interest. She had adjusted her mental state beforehand so that she would appear to be genuinely interested in touring the collection. "The defeat in the Twenty Years' War caused the kingdom to suffer years of humiliation, but it also forged many heroes." Michele resorted to flattery. The White Rose War happened after the Twenty Years' War and before the Battle of the Violated Oath. There, Loen defeated Intis and became strong again. Michele continued introducing his collection as Audrey solemnly listened, occasionally asking questions as she conversed with him. Finally, Michele's finger pointed toward a notebook with a black cover. "This belonged to a knight stationed on Sonia Island in the Twenty Years' War. "This knight's name has already vanished into the long river of history. This notebook is the only proof of his existence. He once held his ground on Sonia Island until the very last moment. "This notebook is not only a firsthand account for research into that portion of history, but it also hides certain problems. The knight's grammar has many uncommon habits. This might be a clue to aid us in determining his exact identity." Audrey instinctively believed that the notebook was her target. Hence, she only leaned in a little. Indeed, the black cover had faint patterns. Together, they outlined an abstract image of a dragon. From Michele's tone and subtle expressions, his interest is focused on the contents rather than the item itself. He doesn't particularly treasure it... I have a good chance of purchasing it... Audrey calmly made her assessment. Turning her head, she smiled at Michele Deuth and asked, "What exactly are those uncommon habits?" "He favors short sentences--very simple, concise ones..." Michele explained with a hint of ostentation. Audrey was always a good listener. She smiled at him and listened attentively. This made Michele speak more. As she listened, she suddenly felt that the knight's grammatical habits were somewhat familiar. That is... Audrey's eyes darted around slightly as she quickly remembered the source of the familiarity. This was a grammatical habit of Dragonese which she had diligently mastered!
Chapter 642: Killing Three Birds With One Stone A knight who knew Dragonese and even used it during the critical period of his development... No wonder the Psychology Alchemists wish to obtain the notebook he left behind... Audrey understood at once and reined in her wandering thoughts. She cheerfully but earnestly discussed the implications of such grammatical habits with Michele Deuth. Soon, they concluded the discussion over the notebook as Michele began introducing the other items. As time passed, the tour slowly drew to a close. Audrey had planned to raise her request to purchase the notebook at their next meeting, making her goal less obvious. However, amid the friendly atmosphere and natural flow of their conversation, she keenly sensed an opportunity. Hence, using the powers of Lie, she made her cheeks flush red. "Mr. Deuth, that helmet from the Sauron royal family, dating back to the White Rose War, reminds me of my ancestors. Pardon my presumption, but may I buy it from you? I would also like the notebook from the Twenty Years' War. I'm deeply impressed by the knight who stood fast on Sonia Island and would like to have it as well. "I know it's not a polite request, but I hope you can understand how I feel. Of course, you have the right to decline." Her eyes visibly darted about, partly deliberate and partly genuine, conveying her uncertainty and embarrassment. Michele subconsciously moved his gaze away as he said slowly in a hoarse voice, "I'm a collector. I won't sell my collection." Neither his tone nor his wording is firm enough... According to the information I gathered earlier, he's a gentleman who values his reputation greatly. He probably finds the idea of selling his collection for cash unacceptable... The Psychology Alchemists likely didn't have someone else complete the mission partly because I needed a way to earn contribution points and partly because they had considered the associate professor's attitude toward such matters... I have to change my approach. Before the visit, Audrey had carefully devised different tests based on the intelligence she had received. After some thought, she changed the subject. "Mr. Deuth, I heard that you're requesting Stoen University to build an ancient relic research center?" "Yes, that has been my goal for the past few years." Michele looked at Audrey and answered frankly. Audrey smiled faintly and said, "I'm very interested in the research in this area. I also feel a deep respect for you and hope to see your wish fulfilled. "Well, I'm planning on donating 1,000 pounds, a nearby piece of land spanning 2,000 ares [1], and a manor with rather good returns to your faculty at Stoen University. I hope to have a non-profit historical relic research and preservation foundation set up. I know it's not a lot, but I will drum up support from the ladies and gentlemen I know in order to persuade them to contribute as well. "Mr. Deuth, I think you're the most professional relic collector and researcher I know. I'm wondering if you're willing to be the person in charge of this non-profit foundation?" Two thousand ares of land near the university. That's worth about 6,000 pounds. Together with the manor and the cash, Miss Audrey would be donating nearly 10,000 pounds... With such a nonprofit foundation for the research and preservation of relics, it would be far easier to secure approval for my research grants... Michele paused for a few seconds before revealing a sincere smile. He bowed solemnly and said, "My honorable lady, the importance you place on academia has deeply moved me. Its radiance matches your beauty and refinement. I believe I have no reason to reject your invitation. "I've already recorded the contents of the notebook. I will send it and the helmet to your residence tonight. Treat it as a gift from a sincere friend." Success! Audrey was delighted as she wished to praise herself. However, she appeared reserved and indifferent. She didn't do anything improper. "It's my honor," she said earnestly. Although the two items were definitely not worth 10,000 pounds, it wouldn't result in any loss on her part. In her plans, this proposal accomplished three important goals and yielded three returns! The first goal was naturally to obtain the item and complete the mission. She would then successfully obtain the Hypnotist potion formula from the Psychology Alchemists. The second goal was to enhance her prestige, standing, and image by donating to academic research and the preservation of ancient relics. This was something most nobles and tycoons needed to do. Even if the donation wasn't today, Audrey would have to donate 3,000 pounds or more to the various charitable organizations. Therefore, she believed that her father, Earl Hall, wouldn't stop her from doing this with a few of her properties. The third goal was to establish a foundation focused on researching and preserving ancient relics, making it easier for her to come into contact with valuable historical records or mysterious items. Audrey didn't need to do anything personally. All she needed to do was sit at home and receive items that might benefit her. It was equivalent to using 10,000 pounds to leverage even more money and establish her own "faction." Of course, if Michele Deuth hadn't accepted this exchange, then she had other plans. The kingdom's Higher Education Commission included a member of the Hall family, as well as noble friends she knew. As long as the associate professor had anything he needed, she was certain that she had the means to satisfy him. However, Audrey didn't like such methods. She had a nagging feeling that they were underhanded and would harm the public interest. After discussing the matter, Audrey stayed for a little longer and chatted idly for about fifteen minutes. This kept the visit from ending too sharply or abruptly. Afterward, she left Michele's house and rode her carriage back to the Hall family's villa in Stoen City. Past eight in the evening, she received the Sauron royalty's helmet and the notebook from the Twenty Years' War. Audrey wore a pair of white-silk gloves and sat before her desk with keen interest. She placed the helmet to the side as she began flipping through the contents of the notebook. She discovered that the entries were sparse. The early entries described how the knight stationed on the ancient elven island had learned to brew Sonia blood wine, pursued women, and passed the tedious days. The later entries covered the Twenty Years' War. They mainly included his curses against the Feysacians, complaints about his companions, and thoughts about his resolve to stand fast. They also included a final account of the initial fall of Sonia Island. Apart from the grammatical habits being similar to Dragonese, there aren't any serious problems. Nor can I find any hidden clues... Audrey frowned as she closed the notebook. She had used methods derived from mysticism to do her checks, but they were to no avail. This made her unwilling to waste time as she planned to turn it over to the Psychology Alchemists. As her thoughts raced, she suddenly had a new idea. Mr. World and Mr. Hanged Man often consider problems from different angles to provide suggestions. Should I learn from them? Well... Looking at it from another angle, if the notebook's contents aren't unusual, could the physical object itself be what the Psychology Alchemists are after? What's so special about it? I didn't discover anything... It belongs to a knight who's accustomed to using Dragonese. That knight must've experienced something... Divination! Yes, divination! Perhaps I can find the knight's final location using divination with the help of the notebook. And this might be related to a dragon! Since it's a dragon, there's a high chance that it's a mind dragon, a representative of the Spectator pathway. Clues involving it would indeed be something the Psychology Alchemists would pay close attention to... Audrey, that's some nice thinking! Audrey's eyes turned crystal clear as it seemed to hide a clear resplendence. She couldn't help turning her head to look at the golden retriever sitting by the side. Susie glanced at her owner and barked. "Audrey, do you want me to praise you?" "No, there's no need..." Audrey turned her head back, feeling a little embarrassed. Then, she discovered an important question. She wasn't able to divine things herself, or it could be said that the revelation that she received from divination would be highly inaccurate! There's no way to confirm it... No, I can seek Mr. Fool's help! A secret deed ritual? It can only be performed on my body, not on an external object... Artificial sleepwalking? It's similar to a secret deed ritual, so that wouldn't work either... Sacrifice it to Mr. Fool and have "Him" perform the divination before bestowing it back upon me? No, that won't work. It would be rather disrespectful. "He" isn't my father or teacher, but a true god. Such a method is far too casual and somewhat sacrilegious... Audrey's thoughts gradually shifted from Mr. Fool to divination. Although she was poor at divination, she had a certain level of understanding in the relevant knowledge. She soon locked onto a particular method of divination. It involved drawing upon the power of a third party--an unknown or mysterious existence--through a particular ritual. The classic example of such a method was magic mirror divination! Yes... It's indeed very dangerous, but the danger stems from the possibility that the target might be malicious or capable of making a person break down instantly. But I don't have such worries. I can seek Mr. Fool's help! Audrey blinked and suppressed her excitement as she said to the golden retriever, "Susie, guard the door outside. I'm going to use a mysticism technique to study this notebook." "Didn't you use those methods already?" Susie asked, puzzled. She's getting harder to fool... Audrey's eyes darted around as she said confidently, "I plan on using magic mirror divination. "Don't worry. I'll make the plea to a safe existence." "Alright." Susie determined that Audrey was speaking the truth. She took a few steps before turning around to exhort her. "Audrey, you need to be careful about being possessed by a mysterious existence." "I know," Audrey replied without feeling worried at all. From her point of view, if Mr. Fool really wanted to do something to her, he had countless opportunities in the past. There was no reason for him to wait until this day. After Susie opened the door, went out, and closed it behind her, Audrey sat at her desk and recited The Fool's honorific name to request permission to use magic mirror divination. After a while, Klein, who was on the Future, went to the bathroom and went above the gray fog. There, he heard Miss Justice's prayer. That works? That's right. As a mysterious and unknown existence, I can serve as the third-party power in a magic mirror divination... Amused, Klein granted her request. Audrey immediately picked up the notebook, sat in front of the dresser, and lit a candle while facing the mirror. 1. Author's Note: One are is 100 square meters. In the late Victorian era, land in the suburbs was approximately 100-130 pounds per acre. Converting to ares, it's about 2 pounds and 10 shillings to 3 pounds and 5 shillings per are. Well, that's excluding London. Of course, this might not be too accurate. I did an inference from the overall cost of the land purchase and building a house and subtracted the cost of building a house from the information from that era.
Chapter 643: Klein's Version of "Magic Mirror Divination" With the curtains tightly drawn and all the lights in the room extinguished, Audrey completed the preparations required for magic mirror divination. Of course, she didn't choose a particular time, as there was no need to go to such trouble when getting Mr. Fool's help. Looking at the candles and their reflected light, as well as her own reflection, Audrey picked up a bottle of extract with excitement and a touch of unease. She dripped a few drops onto the dim flame. As the mild and refreshing fragrances filled her nose, for some inexplicable reason, Audrey recalled the times when she was still a mysticism enthusiast. In the beginning, she had made all kinds of mistakes. At critical moments during rituals, she would realize that she had forgotten to prepare the essential oils and extracts that would please the deity. All she could do was make do with perfume, and her attempts naturally failed. In fact, according to the information Mr. Fool shared, "He" would still respond even if I used perfume... Audrey exhaled softly and used Cogitation to calm herself. She knew that her uncontrolled thoughts weren't ordinary behavior coming from her. The tiny bit of anticipation and nervousness had been magnified by Lie! After making sure she was in an optimal state of mind, Audrey clasped her hands and pressed them to her mouth and nose as if in prayer. She sincerely chanted softly, "The Fool that does not belong to this era. "The mysterious ruler above the gray fog. "The King of Yellow and Black who wields good luck." The secret incantation echoed softly seven times, and Audrey sensed something indescribable lurking in the surrounding darkness, like an undercurrent hidden beneath the water's surface. Looking up, Audrey extended her right hand, passed it through the still candle flame, and stroked the mirror's surface from top to bottom. At this point, the magic mirror divination was basically done. If the mysterious and unknown existence's interest was aroused, it would respond through the mirror. Above the gray fog, in the ancient and magnificent palace, Klein watched the crimson star representing Miss Justice expand and contract, rippling with an illusory glow. Finally, it became tinged with a serenity so deep that it was nearly black and condensed into a mirror-sized circular halo that seemed to lead to the outside world. It's different from past rituals. Interesting... Klein leaned back into his chair and extended his spirituality to make contact with the black circular hole. Silently, his vision changed. The long bronze table and crimson star overlapped with the spacious candlelit room before becoming distinct once again. At that moment, Klein felt that a mirror had become an extension of his body or eye. It allowed him to clearly see and interfere with the real world despite being above the gray fog. Yes, clearly! All the objects in Klein's vision no longer looked blurry as they appeared distinctly in his eyes! His gaze suddenly froze for two seconds. In front of him was a lady in a white, gold-trimmed dress. Her long blonde hair was casually tied up, flowing down in smooth, lustrous waves. Her emerald eyes reflected a somewhat pale flame, appearing as deep as the ocean and as pure as gemstones. Her features and the contours of her face came together in stunning beauty, and her bearing was elegant, clear, and pure. Klein shifted his gaze away as he felt guilty for some inexplicable reason. I nearly mistook her for a rather high-Sequence Demoness. Thankfully, I remembered in time that Miss Justice is a Beyonder of the Spectator pathway. It's impossible for her to become a Demoness... This extract smells quite good. Very distinctive... It has a subtle quality to it. Is that the mystical item made from the Faceless Beyonder characteristic? Miss Justice had it made into a necklace... Klein's gaze landed on the mystical item disguised as a diamond necklace. Then, he heard Miss Justice say with utmost anticipation, "Mirror, Mirror, please tell me the location of the owner of this notebook." Audrey knew that she was asking Mr. Fool, but "Mirror, Mirror" were words she had always wanted to recite from the stories she had heard from a young age. She finally had a chance to use it in practice. My past failures don't count! Yes! Audrey nodded inwardly. Klein instantly looked at the black notebook placed between Miss Justice and the candle. He discovered that his spirituality could easily spread out with the help of the mirror. He could "hold" the divination medium as though he was using his hand. Above the gray fog, he quickly wrote the corresponding divination statement. "The location of the original owner of the notebook." With one "hand" holding the notebook and another hand holding the piece of paper, Klein recited as he leaned back in his chair. With the help of Cogitation, he quickly fell into a deep sleep. Audrey looked at the mirror intently with her emerald eyes, awaiting Mr. Fool's reply. After a few seconds, she saw ripples being produced on the mirror's surface. It worked! Magic mirror divination really worked! Audrey's eyes widened as they reflected the scenes flashing inside the mirror. It was a view of a village from above! The scene zoomed in as the dragon drawings on the various buildings gradually turned clear. A cathedral quickly occupied the mirror in its entirety before being replaced by the cemetery attached to it. Finally, the scene was fixed on a tombstone in a corner. On it were words that had turned blurry as a result of the elements. The only thing that could still be discerned was the name, "Lindelira." At that moment, the mirror suddenly darkened before restoring to normal. It reflected Audrey and the candle in front of her once again. Isn't this the village with the custom of dragon worship? The knight who wrote the notebook was named Lindelira and came from that village. Did he return to his hometown after the defeat in the Twenty Years' War and remain there until his death? Or was his corpse sent home? Hmm... That village is in East Chester County. Stoen City is also part of East Chester County, so it makes perfect sense that the notebook Associate Professor Michele obtained came from there... There really is a mind dragon living in the sea of collective subconscious there... Enlightened, Audrey thanked Mr. Fool and ended the magic mirror divination. Under the candlelight's illumination, she stared at the notebook for a moment before deciding to hand it over. She wanted to know what the Psychology Alchemists would divine or figure out. At the very least, I currently lack the strength to make contact with that mind dragon. That's all I can do... Besides, even if the Psychology Alchemists discover something and benefit from it, once I gradually rise through the organization's ranks, some of it will belong to me~ Audrey's mood quickly brightened again. Above the gray fog, Klein rapped the corner of the long bronze table. With Miss Justice's description, he made his judgment. The notebook and the village had something to do with a dragon, and dragons often implied treasure! What a pity. Miss Justice isn't strong enough; otherwise, I would've encouraged her to explore it and pray to the "Sea God" if anything happened, while I supported her through various means. Yes, it's too dangerous for her. It can only be set aside for now... If the Psychology Alchemists don't discover anything, perhaps we can attempt it in the future... Klein suppressed his regret as he recalled the experience of the magic mirror divination. This kind of divination is extremely advantageous for the third party. There's almost no price to pay for connecting to the real world. If I so wished, I could've torn my way out of the mirror in my Spirit Body form! But for the user, it's indeed dangerous. They are exposed to the "gaze" of an unknown existence without any protection. From there, they can be possessed, controlled, cursed, or corrupted... Klein sighed inwardly. He wasn't worried that Miss Justice would abuse magic mirror divination, as she had the best and safest target to pray to. There was no need for her to seek anyone else. And that would be me! Klein retracted his finger and sat at the end of the long bronze table and waited in silence for twenty to thirty seconds. Soon, he returned to the real world. He didn't stay too long since he was on the Future. There was someone watching him from the dark. After leaving the bathroom and putting away Azik's copper whistle and Will Auceptin's paper crane, Klein glanced at the crimson moon which had been shrouded by clouds as he pondered silently for a moment. He put on his half top hat, pulled open the door, and went into the corridor. After taking a few steps forward, Klein deliberately slowed his footsteps and glanced at the first room on the left through the corner of his eye. Based on his judgment, the mysterious pair of eyes that were silently observing him and the deck during the day was in that room. Klein walked slower and slower as he nearly stopped in front of the door. He didn't hide the extension of his left palm as he reached for the handle when scenes naturally surfaced in his mind. Not far behind the door was a clothes rack with nothing hanging on it. Faint starlight scattered across the clean floorboards. There was a sense of solitude and serenity that lacked the aura of humans. The windows had opened at some point in time as the sea breeze blew in from the outside, lifting the curtains which weren't too heavy. There's no one there? Klein had planned on probing the area, but he immediately retracted his left palm and walked towards the stairs as though nothing had happened. When he arrived on deck, Klein strolled along the starboard side in the cold night breeze, wearing a cold and casual expression as though he had merely come out for some air. Suddenly, he saw a man sitting ahead of him. The man was wearing dungarees and a white shirt. Frank Lee? Klein continued approaching without stopping. The man sensed something as he turned his body halfway around to look at the person approaching. He was none other than Poison Expert Frank Lee, but his usual smile was gone. Blood-red liquid streamed from the corner of his mouth. Klein pricked up his brows without saying a word. Frank Lee suddenly raised his hands and grabbed a silver-scaled fish that wasn't struggling. He said dejectedly, "It failed... Their lifespan is shorter than I imagined. It's impossible to breed them, even if they are planted in the ground..." As he spoke, he raised the silver-scaled fish in his right hand and bit down on it. That's good... Otherwise, I'd really be afraid of what kind of abominations you might create... So, you're drowning your sorrows in alcohol--no, fish? Klein silently heaved a sigh of relief.
Chapter 644: Laughter Klein couldn't go against his own wishes to console Frank Lee, nor could he bring himself to tell Frank Lee that not being able to breed red wine fish was a good thing. All he could do was pretend that this was a trivial problem and not provide a response. He took two diagonal steps around Frank and went to the starboard rail before gazing out over the undulating sea. By then, the clouds high in the sky had thinned. The crimson moon's moonlight brightened up the rather dark night. In that environment, Klein could make out the nearby scenery. Dark clouds hung low, and he saw a hurricane raging across an unknown swath of sea. Under the illumination of the silver lightning, fine rain danced amidst the wind, forming a scene that resembled the dawn of the apocalypse. Such a terrifying disaster was only a few nautical miles away from the Future, but the Future didn't seem affected. Only the wind had become a little stronger. This is what a safe sea route means--advancing alongside a storm... Without a good navigator, ordinary sailing could send a ship straight into disaster... Klein turned his head to look in the direction the ship was heading. He saw a faint glow shining through the fog. Visibility was extremely poor, making it difficult to tell with the naked eye whether they were in a safe or dangerous zone. Such situations weren't obvious west of Oravi Island. But here, it was common once they took the secret sea route. Klein was just about to retract his gaze when he saw a black, massive object seemingly hiding in the periphery of the storm! A sea monster? He suddenly recalled some of the rumors he had heard at the different bars he had been to. After straying from a safe sea route, it's very easy to encounter all kinds of monsters. Some are enormous and possess tremendous offensive power. Once they surface, they can swallow a ship whole. The Future didn't stop advancing. Before long, it closed the gap between it and the gloomy but massive object. Klein finally managed to discern the entity's appearance and discovered that it wasn't a sea monster, but a gigantic sailboat which was even larger than the Future. The sailboat was nearly two hundred meters long. With its bow and stern raised high, it appeared like a crescent. Its hull was black. The cannons were arranged along its side in three somewhat uneven rows, one above another. Apart from the masts, the structures rising from the deck were similarly tall and massive, at least as high as a five-story building. The ship's strangest feature was that it had only one sail, upon which was the image of a black tomb. "The Death Announcer..." A heavy voice sounded in Klein's ears. At some point, Frank Lee had thrown away the silver-scaled fish whose blood had been replaced by red wine and come to his side. The first mate who had a bounty of 7,000 pounds held his head high as his muscles remained tense. It was as though an attack would be launched anytime at the slightest movement of the gigantic sailboat. Death Announcer? Klein was first taken aback before he recalled what the name represented. It was one of the most legendary and infamous ships on the Five Seas! It was the flagship of the King of Immortality Agalito! We actually encountered one of the Four Kings... Klein clicked his tongue inwardly as he involuntarily went on high alert. However, he maintained a superficial level of indifference and calm as he continued looking at the Death Announcer. Recalling how the second mate of the Death Announcer, Slaughterer Kircheis, who had a bounty of 9,500 pounds, had recently appeared in Nas and warned him, Klein understood. He was no longer puzzled as to why he would bump into the Death Announcer not far from the Gargas Archipelago. Setting that question aside, he recalled even more rumors, several of which had been confirmed as accurate. King of Immortality Agalito is a middle-aged man who's so pale that he's on the brink of rotting at any moment. The bounty placed on him by a single country reached as high as 100,000 pounds. His former enemies are all dead, regardless of whether they were pirates, adventurers, or members of a naval fleet. Only the other three members of the Four Kings remained alive. He has never entered into direct combat with an official demigod. He is extremely restrained in such matters. No one really knows his exact Sequence. No one knows what his Beyonder powers are. He's cruel by nature and enjoys killing. He can launch an attack on any person or any ship at random. He likes finding excuses to break his promises. In addition to being called the King of Immortality, he is often nicknamed "The Untrustworthy." Thankfully, I'm on the Future. The King of Immortality will likely give Admiral of Stars a free pass. After all, she's one of the seven pirate admirals... No, the Four Kings and the Pirate Admirals can ordinarily cooperate or oppose one another, except during the pirate convention organized by the King of the Five Seas... Given the King of Immortality's character, he might leave us no chance of survival! Just as this thought flashed through Klein's mind, he heard a deep, rumbling horn. Whoosh! The sailors resting in the cabins jolted awake. Without even dressing, they ran to the cannons on deck and prepared for battle. The Future instantly went from peaceful to combat-ready. Klein turned his head and looked up. He saw that the captain's windows were already open. Cattleya wore the usual black dress as she stood there and observed the Death Announcer. She wasn't wearing the thick glasses, and her pitch-black eyes were tainted with some purple, making them mysterious and deep. Indeed, she's also worried about a sudden attack from the King of Immortality... Klein retracted his gaze and looked at the Death Announcer with its stern raised high. At that moment, the two ships had just passed each other by. The pirates could see their counterparts on the other ship. The pirates aboard the other ship were also looking over. Silent and motionless as statues, as though devoid of all emotion, they brandished their knives and trained their guns on the Future in an extremely provocative display. At that moment, a single spark would have been enough to ignite the tension and start a battle. Finally, the Death Announcer didn't take any action. It remained silently anchored on the spot, "watching" the Future pass it by before it distanced itself. Phew... At Klein's side, Frank Lee didn't conceal his exhalation. He smiled and said to Klein, "Heh heh, there have always been many rumors about the King of Immortality's strength. Some say he's truly a demigod, while others claim he's only a Sequence 5 who can reach the level of Sequence 4 thanks to the Death Announcer. Regardless, he has lived for a very long time. Uh... Tell me, do you think crossbreeding him with my fish would improve their survivability?" Frank suddenly had an idea. First, you need to capture the King of Immortality, or else make him interested in your fish... Klein lampooned inwardly before saying calmly, "You can discuss it with him." Frank Lee was taken aback as he sighed, depressed. "He won't agree to it. He will plant me into the soil." Just as he said that, the Death Announcer which had fallen behind the Future suddenly turned its sails. Shrill, malicious laughter rang out from several hundred meters away and swept over the Future. "Hahaha! "Hahaha!" The laughter resounded without pause. It shifted from shrill to hoarse to chaotic, at times resembling ravings and at others singing. One after another, the sailors on deck fell to the ground. They desperately covered their ears, but could only struggle in pain. A number of Beyonders began to produce fish scales on their bodies. Klein was similarly affected. He felt that his brain was instantly injected with all kinds of thoughts. There were the good, the bad, the bright, and the dark. Klein's facial expression distorted slightly as inconspicuous flesh tendrils began wriggling under his skin. If he hadn't experienced the True Creator's ravings and Mr. Door's cries for help, or suffered similar torment each time he passed through the gray fog, building a certain degree of resistance, Klein would've ended up like Poison Expert Frank Lee--clutching his head and kneeling with a contorted expression as he resisted the pain brought by the terrifying laughter. Klein noticed that some short orange hair was growing from Frank's face, making him seem to transform into a bear. The terrifying laughter, by turns shrill and hoarse, didn't weaken, but everyone instantly seemed to grow distant from one another. Sounds from farther away became hollow and illusory. Klein's swelling head instantly found relief as he used the rest of his strength to look up. Behind the open windows of the captain's cabin, dark traces had appeared on the Admiral of Stars's face.
