At that moment, Cattleya's palms pressed against the windowsill as bits of starlight swirled around her, seemingly matching the Future which was on the resplendent sea. Whoosh! A squall stirred for no reason as the ship began its own adjustment. Despite the Future having so many of its sailors down, it accelerated instead of slowing. It quickly opened up a gap from the Death Announcer. Klein looked at the room with the mysterious pair of eyes that observed the deck, and he discovered that the windows were rattling from the strong winds without any signs of abnormalities. Whoosh! Amid the strong winds, starlight descended to form a sheet of "floating ice" that dragged the Future into "rapid flight." Finally, the Death Announcer vanished behind it. The terrifying laughter which could make a person lose control or go mad turned more illusory and distant. Frank Lee lowered his hands and panted before barely recovering. Many of the sailors on the deck were still tumbling about and struggling in extreme pain, but their condition didn't worsen. This ability of the King of Immortality is truly impressive. There's almost no way to defend against it... No wonder he's one of the Four Kings... Klein frowned slightly as he sighed. Although he was experienced and rather knowledgeable, this was the first time he had been directly attacked by a demigod in the truest sense. He discovered that even Agalito, ranked last among the Four Kings, made him feel weak and incapable of resistance. With Agalito's character, will he make the Death Announcer pursue us? Although there's a high chance he would wait for Slaughterer Kircheis to return, that possibility cannot be excluded... If he catches up, I'll pray to myself and use the Sea God Scepter to give him a maelstrom and a thunderstorm to wipe him out... After making the decision, he once again looked at Cattleya. The pirate admiral's expression was already ghastly pale. However, there were no longer any signs of darkness. The starlight that twirled around her slowly extinguished one after another.
Chapter 645: Calming Method After the surrounding astral glow completely vanished, Cattleya lowered her head and said to the slowly recovering Frank Lee, "Calm them down." She was referring to the sailors who were still struggling in pain. Just as she said that, Cattleya drew back as the windows closed. At that instant, Klein vaguely saw a green vine grow upward, covering the Admiral of Stars in layers. Since he sensed neither danger nor malevolence, he intuitively believed it was a mysticism technique Ma'am Hermit used to treat her injuries and restore her energy. A power from her Beyonder pathway? Or is it from some mystical item she possesses? She began treating herself without any concern, leaving Frank to deal with the chaos on the ship. Isn't she afraid the Death Announcer will catch up to us? How far did the Future "fly" in that last burst? Klein stopped craning his neck and turned to look at Frank Lee. This first mate, who was both a poison expert and a capable doctor, had already retrieved a coiled soft tube from the pocket of his dungarees. It was connected to a small glass bottle, and on the other side was an embedded thin and sharp needle. "A sedative I concocted," Frank Lee said with a forced smile while still having lingering fear. I've bought something similar before. They were all given to Zombie Maric... Klein surveyed the area and said, "This might not be enough." "No, it isn't for them. I need an assistant. They'll be helped by beer with a sedative effect. Haha, they often get rowdy when they're drunk, so I've added the necessary ingredients to most of the barrels of alcohol," Frank explained casually. Spiking their drinks without telling anyone... The corner of Klein's mouth nearly twitched. At that moment, he had a deep appreciation for the aptness of the nickname "Poison Expert." Simply because he found the pirates rowdy when drunk, Frank had added a modified sedative to most of the alcoholic beverages without any sense of guilt or shame. It was as though he was doing something very ordinary. This fellow is genuinely straightforward and warm in some respects, but in others, he's more terrifying than a devil because he doesn't believe anything he does is evil... How did the Church of the Earth Mother produce such a mad scientist? Klein controlled his expression and followed Frank Lee at a distance until they found Boatswain Nina writhing in the shadows by the bulkhead. This pirate with an exaggerated figure was slumped there, writhing in pain. She kept scratching the deck and producing ear-piercing sounds as bloody marks were left behind. Just watching the scene made Klein feel pain in his fingers. "Gehrman, help me press her down to prevent her from struggling." Frank raised the needle and tube in his hand. Klein didn't object to it, but he didn't say a word. He calmly crouched by the side and pressed down on Nina's shoulders. He felt his hands slip the moment he touched her, finding it difficult to grab her. It was as though she wasn't a lady but a gigantic fish covered in slippery scales. Klein instantly corrected his actions. Using a Clown's precise control, he grabbed Nina firmly by the shoulders. However, Nina's struggles were surprisingly powerful, far stronger than Klein. Soon, his fingers began to ache, and he could barely hold on. As expected of a Sequence 7 Beyonder from the Sailor pathway, while I'm not a Beyonder who excels in physical strength... If not for the need to feed it, I could activate Creeping Hunger, switch to Steel Maveti's soul, and use a Zombie's strength, which would be the most suitable response... As these thoughts ran through his mind, Klein saw Frank approach, crouch down, and press his knee against Nina's back. His muscles bulged as he quickly stopped Nina's struggles. A Beyonder from the Planter pathway possesses considerable physical strength as well... However, Mr. Frank Lee, you'll probably have a hard time finding a girlfriend if you treat a lady so roughly... Of course, you definitely don't mind. You could always grow your child in the soil... Klein lampooned inwardly as he watched Frank Lee insert the needle into the back of Nina's hand. As the small bottle's sedative was injected, Nina stopped her attempts at struggling. Klein released his hands and stood up. After a few seconds, Nina combed her hair and rolled to her feet. She grumbled at Frank Lee, "Why must you always be so rough like a bear? Can't you try a different method?" As she spoke, she stretched her arms without concealing the pained expression on her face. Unlike during her earlier dive, she was now wearing a linen shirt and a brown coat. She looked no different from an ordinary pirate. Frank wasn't fazed by Nina's complaints as he asked, puzzled, "How was I rough? "Alright, let's not argue on this topic. Let's help them first. "Get the beer barrel out. Let's work together to make them drink. "Gehrman, you don't mind participating in this, right?" Klein shot a glance at the sailors on the deck. After contemplating for a few seconds, he asked, "The goal is to let them calm down?" "That's right." Frank Lee nodded heavily. "Can I simply knock them unconscious?" Klein asked calmly. This has almost the same effect as sedative-laced beer, and it's more efficient... he added inwardly. Nina turned her head in surprise and was momentarily stunned speechless. Frank Lee thought seriously for a moment. "Okay." "Alright." Klein walked to a cutlass he had long noticed, picked it up, and struck its owner with the dull edge. Bang! Through his precise control, the pirate who was rolling in pain calmed down and fell unconscious. Nina's expression froze for a second before she recovered. She then slowed as she passed Klein. Suppressing her laughter, she said, "I've heard rumors about you, but I never expected you to be more outrageous than the rumors. Usually, it's the other way around. "Yes... Your way of thinking is very, very unusual. It's completely different from everyone else's and closer to Frank's. That's probably why he came to regard you as a friend so quickly." No, there are differences even among lunatics. Gehrman Sparrow hasn't reached Frank's level yet... Klein observed silently and replied inwardly. Ignoring Nina, he carried the cutlass across the deck, knocking the sailors unconscious so they could wake naturally. Frank wanted to do the same, but abandoned the rash idea when Nina asked whether he could guarantee that he would only knock them unconscious rather than kill them. He entered the cabin, brought out a barrel of beer, and proceeded with his original plan. Bam! Bam! Bam! Klein struck as he walked all the way to the bow. At that moment, an elder in his fifties with a pointed bonnet had gradually come around. When he saw the cold and crazy adventurer approach, he hurriedly tried to stand up and blurted out, "No, I don't need it! "I'm already fine. I'm fine!" There's no need to explain. It's very clear... Klein held back his amusement and turned for the bow. At that moment, the elder introduced himself, "I'm the navigator of the Future, Ottolov." Navigator? Klein turned his head and discovered several books dropped around Ottolov. They were either spread on the ground face up or down, flat or sideways. "Haha, I fell from above and brought them with me. They nearly went mad," Ottolov explained. Klein shifted his gaze to Ottolov's eyes and discovered a deep-sea hue in their blue depths. It's not the pair of eyes that were observing me in the day... But this feeling is somewhat similar to the Admiral of Stars... They are of the same pathway? Klein retracted his gaze and watched Nina and Frank Lee calm the other sailors. Just as he was about to look back to see if the Death Announcer had continued its pursuit, Ottolov suddenly shouted, "Be careful!" Whoosh! A huge wave struck the bow, causing the Future to shake vigorously. If not for his balancing ability as a Clown, Klein would've fallen like Frank had. And when the huge spray pattered down like rain, it drenched his half top hat and double-breasted frock coat. There should be a steam iron here, right... A crazy adventurer washing his clothes doesn't violate his persona. It would be strange if he didn't wash them... I should've worn clothes in the style of the Rorsted Archipelago natives! At that moment, Klein felt a pang of heartache. He saw a storm ahead with huge waves coming one after another as they surged high up like mountains. He could sense the crazy winds and the rumbling thunder. W-we've reached the boundary of the safe sea route? That "flight" might've allowed us to shake off the Death Announcer, but it also sent the ship off course? Klein watched as Ottolov, Nina, Frank, and Bloodless Heath Doyle, who had appeared at some point, roused the sailors and took their positions. They frantically set about steering the Future. Through their efforts, the Future changed direction in time, cut through the gigantic waves, and dodged the bolts of lightning before returning to the safe sea route. After everything calmed down, Klein released the Sea God domain charm and breathed a sigh of relief. Looking back, he saw no sign of the Death Announcer pursuing them. He finally relaxed, reflecting that there had been nothing peaceful about the night. After surveying the pirates as they rubbed their heads or gasped for breath, exhausted and on the verge of collapse, Klein left the deck with a faint sense of guilt. He entered the cabin and sighed inwardly. We only recently left the Gargas Archipelago, and the ship was nearly destroyed. The search for mermaids really isn't going to be simple... Following the staircase to the upper level, Klein walked past the captain's cabin and slowed down. He observed for a moment and saw green leaves covering the crack in the door. Everything was isolated. He shifted his gaze and returned to his room. He considered praying to The Fool, going above the gray fog, and responding to the prayer to gain an overview of the nearby waters and search for traces of the Death Announcer. He wanted King of Immortality Agalito, who attacked others for no reason, to have a taste of his own medicine. No, there are "eyes" watching. I should try my best not to do such things. Besides, it will only teach the King of Immortality a lesson and not seriously injure him. It's not worth the risk... I shouldn't let my anger get the better of my rationality... I'll think about it again after advancing successfully! Klein repressed his urge.
Chapter 646: Leymano's Spellbook Backlund, outside the steam locomotive station. Fors wore a finely checkered black veiled hat decorated with blue flowers and stood in the hall at the station entrance, awaiting her teacher, Dorian Gray. The street drizzle and the cold drafts blowing through it made the female author tremble slightly. She felt that she had underestimated Backlund's spring. I wonder what Xio is doing that makes her busy all year round. Sigh, she said that she wouldn't even get out of bed when her father was still alive. Apart from going to the bathroom, both food and water would be served to her by her servants. Now, she's leaving early in the morning every day and only returning late at night regardless of the weather. She has completed one mission after another, capturing one fugitive after another. With this in mind, Fors couldn't help but admire Xio. Last week, this female Sheriff had already paid off her debt and had even saved up 200 pounds! I have to say, Sheriff is a Beyonder profession perfectly suited to bounty hunting. Of course, her choices are limited to Low-Sequence Beyonders... As Fors's thoughts wandered, her outward gaze suddenly caught sight of a familiar figure. It was a man of medium build, and he was dressed in a black suit, the most popular attire in Loen. He wore a half top hat, and unusually, his shoulders appeared broad. They were broad in an almost exaggerated sense. He was none other than Fors's teacher, one of the few remaining members of the Abraham family, Dorian Gray Abraham. Fors was delighted as she immediately went over with her umbrella in hand. With so many people on the street, she didn't approach him directly. However, their gazes met, and she saw him raise his clenched right fist toward the first button of his black suit. This... means danger! Fors diverted her gaze without changing her expression. Smiling, she looked at a young gentleman behind Dorian and walked past him as though nothing had happened. An ancient family possessed unimaginable experience in all kinds of matters, so Dorian Gray had long since taught Fors the signals and gestures to use in emergencies. The previous gesture had a very simple meaning: stay away! The young man behind was somewhat taken aback to be stared at by the languid, mature lady. He instinctively adjusted his clothes and pressed down on his hat. Just as he finished this series of actions, Fors had overtaken him and continued heading forward. In the drizzle, Fors circled the area, boarded a rental carriage, and headed to the Hat Trick Inn at 22 Hope Street in Cherwood Borough. Dorian Gray had reserved a room there in advance. Having spent so many years in mysticism circles, the experienced Fors calmly rented a neighboring room and stood by the window to observe the guests entering the inn. Finally, she saw Dorian Gray get off a carriage and walk through the door. Fors quickly turned around and came to the bend of the stairwell. She covertly observed her teacher being led to his room by an attendant. After a while, she took off her hat and mussed her hair before going to Room 2016 and knocking. Her plan was very simple. If her teacher's response wasn't problematic, she would enter the room to converse with him. If it was abnormal, she would pretend as though she had come to the wrong room or that she was a prostitute trying to get some business. Creak. The door slowly opened as Dorian looked at his student in front of him before looking both ways down the corridor. Then, he raised his right arm and spread his fingers to press on the second button of his suit. This meant that he wasn't controlled and that the abnormality was over. Fors let out a silent sigh of relief and instantly entered the room. "Teacher, what happened just now?" she asked, feeling worried and concerned. Dorian closed the door and smiled wryly. "I saw someone familiar." He sighed and added, "An enemy." It was his former student who had later betrayed the Abraham family with Traveler Boulaya and nearly wiped out the upper echelons of the Abraham family. According to what Dorian knew, his former student had already joined the Aurora Order and was likely one of the 22 Oracles. "What did he do? Is he very strong?" Fors asked curiously. Dorian fell silent for a few seconds and divulged a little. "Lawrence, Laubero, Aulisa, and I belong to a particular organization. A few members betrayed it and dealt a heavy blow to it. "That was one of the traitors." He didn't describe it as a family, nor did he mention the conflict between bloodline members and apprentices, lest Fors become emotionally involved. "How despicable!" Fors immediately recalled the kind Mrs. Aulisa and the friendly and amiable Mr. Lawrence. "Alright, let's not chat about such unhappy matters." Dorian took out a piece of paper that had been folded a few times and handed it to Fors. "Here's the Astrologer potion formula. Your digestion of the Trickmaster and Apprentice potions has exceeded my expectations. This is the greatest surprise I've had in the past ten years." "I specially joined a circus." Fors didn't hide the fact, and she even felt that it was worth flaunting. As she spoke, she unfolded the piece of paper to read the Astrologer's potion formula. At that moment, Dorian nodded in relief. "I'm very sorry. Due to our previous losses, I'm unable to provide you with the main ingredients of the Astrologer potion. Treat obtaining them as a final test. "However, I have prepared a gift for you." As he spoke, he took out a palm-sized book from his inner left pocket. Its cover looked hard, and it was entirely bronze-green in color. It looked rather ancient. The notebook contained three types of paper. The yellow parchment had the fewest pages, there were about ten pages of yellowish-brown goatskin, and the rest were ordinary white paper. Written on the cover in ancient Feysac were the words: "I came, I saw, I recorded." Fors's gaze moved away from the Astrologer potion formula and onto the notebook. She recognized it to be the item left behind by Mr. Lawrence. It was the item she had specially traveled all the way to Pritz Harbor to hand to her teacher! Dorian smiled. "I believe you are no stranger to it." After Fors nodded, he sighed. "This is a rather powerful mystical item. It ranks among the top five similar items I've seen. That doesn't mean it's more powerful than everything ranked below it, but its negative effects are among the easiest to mitigate. Taken together, that makes it extremely valuable." "What is its name? What negative side effects does it have?" Fors couldn't disguise her excitement and agitation. Dorian caressed the notebook's cover and said, "It's called 'Leymano's Travels,' but we prefer calling it 'Leymano's Spellbook.' "This spellbook not only gives you access to more kinds of Beyonder powers, but also allows you to record them. "The power will materialize on a particular page for long-term storage. You can use it at any time, but remember that after each use, the corresponding page will become blank again and await your next recording." It sounds amazing. Fors felt as though she was dreaming. I can record any Beyonder powers I see and use them once? I-isn't this another kind of Shepherd? The Shepherd mentioned by Little Sun... Yes, it's only limited to a single prepared battle. I wonder if I can record the Beyonder powers of a demigod. If it's possible, in a prepared battle, I'll be even stronger than a Shepherd! Dorian seemed to read her mind as he explained in detail. "You could say that. It corresponds to a Sequence 6 Scribe of the Apprentice pathway. Recording a Beyonder power above that Sequence isn't guaranteed to succeed. The greater the gap, the greater the chance of failure. Furthermore, the power's effects will be halved. "According to the experience of past users, while the chance of successfully recording a Sequence 5 Beyonder power is considerably high, once it reaches Sequence 4, which is the level of a demigod, it becomes relatively difficult. There might not be a single instance of success within ten attempts. And I believe no demigod will use it again and again for you. If it's an enemy, they'd have killed you ten times over. "Do you see these? The yellow parchment pages are specifically used to record Beyonder powers with godhood. There are a total of three pages, which is to say that even if you are very lucky, you can record at most three demigod Beyonder powers, and you can only use them each once." Although it appears to have many restrictions that make it impossible to bring out the traveling notebook's full might, they aren't obstacles for two types of people: someone extremely lucky, or someone backed by a large organization or faction with a demigod willing to help... Fors instantly thought of asking Mr. Fool to display "His" powers so she could record them. However, she immediately found the thought sacrilegious and hurriedly apologized inwardly. Afterward, she sincerely hoped that the supposedly strongest Ma'am Hermit in the Tarot Club would quickly become a demigod. Dorian noticed that Fors's thoughts were wandering and continued, "The goatskin pages can record the Beyonder powers of Sequence 5 or 6. There are ten pages in total, and the recorded powers retain more than half their original effects, roughly 70 to 80%. "The remaining pages can record Beyonder powers below Sequence 6. There are 25 pages in total, and the recorded powers are almost as effective as the originals, though still slightly inferior. "Due to past events, the spellbook still has five pages with Beyonder powers left. The rest are blank. You can test them for yourself." Dorian paused before saying solemnly, "Before giving it to you, I must warn you about its negative effects. Each time you use it, it will cause you to lose your way, and in a manner that leads you into danger. You have to draw a little blood and smear it evenly across the cover to reduce the effects. "Remember, don't underestimate getting lost. You must resolve it as quickly as possible." "Yes, Teacher," Fors replied seriously. Dorian then handed Leymano's Travels to Fors. "This is my gift." Teacher is so kind... Fors pursed her lips and asked, "What's the name of the student who betrayed you? What does he look like? "If there's a chance, I wish to seek vengeance on him for both you and Mr. Lawrence." "No, don't think about it. You are much weaker than him. Back when he betrayed us, he was already a Scribe. Now, he might even be a Traveler," Dorian said solemnly. "However, you do need to remember him and avoid him. His name is Lewis Wien. I'll draw a picture of him later." "Alright." Fors nodded. On the Future, in the pirates' dining hall. Klein met Cattleya who was exiting just as he walked in. The lady was no longer as pale as the previous night. With a pair of thick glasses, she calmly said, "Make your preparations. We will be arriving in those waters in a while." That fast? How far exactly did we fly last night? Klein was taken aback.
Chapter 647: Sea of Ruins Although Gehrman Sparrow showed nothing on his face, Cattleya seemed to notice his surprise. She simply explained, "It's a kind of flight that makes it impossible for the Death Announcer to continue pursuing us." As she said this, she noticed that Gehrman Sparrow had changed his entire outfit. He wore a round-necked shirt, a brown jacket, pantaloons, and a dark-colored cap. He no longer looked like an adventurer, instead resembling a native of the City of Generosity, Bayam. According to Nina, his clothes were drenched by a huge wave last night... Does he own only one decent set of clothes? Cattleya remembered the incident and understood. She wasn't surprised. She even felt that it suited Gehrman Sparrow's madness. He owned only one decent set of clothes and spent the rest of his money on mystical items, Beyonder weapons, and spirituality charms--all for the sole purpose of increasing his strength. No wonder the King of Immortality gave up. He merely attacked a passing ship. There wasn't enough hatred to drive him to pursue us all the way... Yes, even against the Four Kings, senior pirate admirals still have some chance of escaping... We're almost there... Man, I haven't finished digesting the potion... However, acting as a crazy adventurer yesterday seemed rather effective. The crew of the Future responded very spontaneously and enthusiastically. I should completely digest the potion in two or three days. And even after we enter the dangerous waters, finding mermaids won't be that simple. I should have enough time... Klein nodded and suppressed his urge to ask. He planned to walk past Admiral of Stars and head toward his usual spot for breakfast. At that moment, he saw a pirate rush in carrying a blue fish that was alive and thrashing. The pirate went straight to a corner. Seated there was the Future's second mate, Heath Doyle. His face was so pale as to be nearly translucent, and the bridge of his nose looked oddly out of proportion. Thud! The fish which was nearly a meter long was placed in front of Bloodless. Heath Doyle extended his hands and pressed down on the fish. He bent his body bit by bit as he inched his head downwards, pressing his face to the scales as though he was kissing it. Suddenly, the fish stiffened and, like wax meeting fire, melted rapidly and turned into a disgusting pool of flesh and blood. The flesh and blood liquefied, surging into Heath Doyle's mouth and flowing over his skin. Amid the horrific squirming, the entire fish--bones, flesh, and blood--vanished. Nothing remained, and Heath Doyle's face was perfectly clean. Only his lips were left bright red, like a blooming rose. Rose Bishop... The name of the Sequence surfaced in Klein's mind. Cattleya, who was beside him, also saw the scene as she nudged her glasses. "Every Rose Bishop needs to replenish themselves with sufficient flesh and blood. That way, they can fully display their Beyonder powers and avoid losing control after being injured in an intense battle. Her lips curled slightly as she added, "However, the lunatics from the Aurora Order have a preference for human flesh and blood. In fact, substitutes work just as well." From the looks of it, this Bloodless, with a bounty of 7,600 pounds, is truly lucky. For one thing, he was fortunate enough to become a Sequence 6 in a single step without suffering any abnormalities or losing control. For another, he joined Admiral of Stars's pirate crew. Without the secret knowledge possessed by this lady pursued by knowledge, he might've turned into a monster craving human flesh and blood sooner or later, even if he never listened to the True Creator's voice... Klein sighed silently. He was increasingly convinced that the Secrets Suppliant pathway, which led to Shepherd, was the Beyonder pathway most prone to losing control and going mad. Nothing else came close; even the Abyss pathway, which represented evil, fell slightly short. Klein retracted his gaze, and just as he was about to take a step forward, the entire ship jolted. In an instant, the scene ahead of the Future naturally surfaced in Klein's mind. A gigantic crack split the blue sea, and an immense volume of seawater plummeted like a waterfall into the bottomless darkness! This scene was magnificent and mystical. It made one wonder whether they were still on Earth. Whoosh! The Future wasn't able to stop in time as it rushed to the edge and quickly plummeted. Bang! Bang! Bang! All the pirates in the dining hall flew up and slammed into the ceiling. Toast, white bread, butter, margarine, beer, and roasted fish flew wildly through the air. Klein also lost his balance as he couldn't help but be thrown toward the ceiling. He extended his palm in time and pushed against the ceiling, swiftly adjusting his posture with an acrobatic maneuver so that he appeared less pathetic. Not far away, Nina displayed her remarkable balance, using the ceiling to steady herself. Whether intentionally or not, she kicked Frank, sending the Poison Expert flying diagonally into a beer barrel and drenching him in pale yellow liquid. At that moment, Cattleya was the calmest and least affected. Stars swirled around her as radiance coalesced beneath her feet, causing her to float in midair, unaffected by the sudden plunge. Apart from her, Bloodless was least disheveled. At some point in time, this Rose Bishop had blended into the shadows and disappeared. With the Future about to plummet into the bottomless crevice, a plume of water surged up suddenly! It caught the ship and hurled it high into the air toward the opposite edge. After a moment in the air, Klein felt the Future land steadily on the sea's surface. Once again, the Sea God domain charm clutched tightly in his right hand went unused. At that moment, the sunlight outside the window shone inside, illuminating the mess inside the dining hall. Klein, who had long regained his balance, briskly walked to the window and saw that the endless sea seemed to be burning with golden flames. It appeared to have been noon the entire time. It was only morning moments ago! Klein looked up and narrowed his eyes to see that the sky was filled with sunlight. There were no clouds nor the sun, just a swath of golden rays. No wonder Arrodes described this place as no longer an ordinary ocean, but a relic of a war between the gods. Sweeping his gaze around, he discovered nearby ruins ahead and off to one side. The ruins were mostly submerged. Gray rocks and stone columns protruded from the surface, forming a peak crowned by a dome-like structure. Judging from its curvature, it had once enclosed a vast space. The ruins had clearly been massive in their prime. Through the clear water, Klein saw their foundations extend endlessly toward the seabed. "These are extremely dangerous waters." At some point in time, Cattleya came beside him. Klein turned his head over and waited for her to continue. Cattleya's gaze was cast forward as she said somewhat wistfully, "I haven't been here many times. Furthermore, all my visits happened a long time ago." "My," not "our"... That means she wasn't with the Future's crew... Was it back when she was Queen Mystic's subordinate? Klein keenly noticed Admiral of Stars's choice of words and formed a hypothesis. Cattleya didn't turn her head as she looked at the sky and sea which were covered in golden flames. "No one knows where these waters end, nor how vast they are. "Do you know what's most dangerous about this place?" I should've gotten Arrodes to give me a more detailed explanation... Klein honestly shook his head. Previously, he had nearly been caught by a demigod of the True Creator. He had only survived thanks to the Die of Probability; therefore, in the past two months, he didn't dare bring the radio transceiver back to the real world. He was afraid that the True Creator, who was closely watching the region, would sense it. Hence, he didn't have an opportunity to contact Arrodes. His original plan had been to seek Will Auceptin's help through the paper crane once he approached the dangerous waters, so he could understand the hazards of the environment. To his surprise, they had encountered King of Immortality Agalito, and the Future had arrived at its destination before giving him any time to prepare. Behind the thick glasses, Cattleya's black eyes with a purple hue glazed over for a moment. "Many ruins float here, along with all kinds of mutated monsters. Among them are numerous demigods who have lost control and ancient evil creatures. "That isn't the most dangerous part. If that were all, these waters would've become a hunting ground for the seven Churches, a treasure trove where they could obtain High-Sequence ingredients or items. Of course, many monsters and evil creatures here have lost control, but some of them might not be real. They can kill us, yet might leave nothing behind when killed." Upon hearing this, Klein made the connection to the Dragon of Imagination, Ankewelt. This dragon king could conjure anything through his imagination! Could it be that these waters were where the ancient gods of the Second Epoch fought? Klein nearly frowned. Cattleya continued in an ethereal voice, "Here, you can never guess what danger you'll encounter next. Perhaps you'll melt while approaching a ruin and turn into a waxlike monster. Perhaps a slight deviation from the explored sea routes will cause you to turn to stone amid a storm and shatter into pieces. "To Beyonders at our level, that is the greatest danger." Klein turned his head slightly and asked pointedly, "What about Beyonders above our level?" Cattleya sighed and smiled. "The waters here are filled with a voice that shouldn't be heard. "The higher the Sequence, the easier it is to hear it. Therefore, most demigods who dare explore these waters have ended up with problems. They either went mad or lost control, ending up lost here forever." No wonder the seven Churches don't send their experts here to reap the harvest... Most of them ended up in trouble... Does that mean a small number of demigods can survive here? Understanding dawned on Klein as he looked out the window again. At that moment, the Future had closed in on the ruins. Suddenly, everyone heard loud, distinct panting!
Chapter 648: Noon and Night Whoosh! Gasp! The loud panting entered Klein's ears in a slow, steady rhythm. A chill ran down his spine, filling him with an inexplicable sense of horror, yet he sensed no premonition of danger. He wasn't the only one. Cattleya, Frank Lee, and the other pirates also heard the panting. They turned their heads, looked outside, raised their weapons, or went on high alert, displaying their extensive experience. After trying to discern its source, Klein discovered that the intense panting came from the ruins ahead, from somewhere amid the peak formed by rocks and stone columns. At that moment, Bloodless Heath Doyle floated out of the shadows. He clasped his head and softly grunted in pain. "There's a corpse... There's a corpse there!" A corpse? One that pants loudly? Klein's thoughts raced. Cattleya had subconsciously removed her thick glasses to look toward the ruins, and her expression suddenly turned solemn. She turned toward the pirates in the dining hall and said, "Quick! "Quickly circle around that area and do not approach it!" Her voice carried a magnetic allure that jolted everyone awake. The sailors rushed out of the dining hall and headed wherever help was needed. Under the instructions of Navigator Ottolov and Boatswain Nina, they adjusted the sails and changed course, passing the ruins at a considerable distance. Only when the peak formed by rocks and stone columns vanished beyond the horizon did Bloodless Heath Doyle lower his hands, the pain gone from his expression. Upon seeing this, Klein narrowed his eyes. He felt that this Rose Bishop, the Future's second mate, might pose an enormous latent risk on the voyage. This wasn't due to contempt for Beyonders of the Secrets Suppliant pathway, but was a judgment based on the Admiral of Stars's description and Heath Doyle's reaction. Although everyone had heard the loud panting, Heath Doyle had been the only one in pain. He instinctively believed a corpse was buried in the ruins, and Cattleya's reaction after observing them proved him right. That means that even if Heath Doyle doesn't actively listen to the True Creator's voice, merely possessing the Beyonder powers of a Listener is enough for him to hear more than ordinary people and most Low- and Mid-Sequence Beyonders under normal circumstances. Hence, when we were close enough to the source of the panting, he was affected the most and learned more about the danger. Here, the problem can't be solved merely by avoiding similar ruins. According to Cattleya, these waters are filled with voices that can make a demigod lose control--voices that shouldn't be heard. If Heath Doyle's condition were poor or he became overly receptive, he might end up hearing those lethal whispers. Similarly, even if a Sequence 6 Rose Bishop is inferior to a demigod skilled at listening, the gap can't be too great. In terms of the Die of Probability, just 2 points--not even 1--would be enough to make Heath Doyle hear voices he shouldn't and go mad or lose control... I have to warn Ma'am Hermit, even though she should've realized this long ago and made the necessary preparations... Klein retracted his gaze and heard his stomach growl softly. He had yet to eat breakfast. Beer covered the floor, and butter was splattered everywhere. All kinds of food--roasted fish, toast, and white bread--lay scattered across the floor or hung from various objects. All of it was somewhat dirty. It should still be edible if I peel off the outer layer... Klein looked at a piece of bread leaning against a table leg, torn over what to do. This was at odds with Gehrman Sparrow's persona! As he decided to wait for lunch, Cattleya instructed the chef, "Prepare another breakfast for everyone. "Leave this to Frank. P-perhaps he has uses for it." For the rearing of monsters? Klein lampooned inwardly. After a while, he finally received a breakfast that wasn't as sumptuous as the first: a smoked pork sausage, two thoroughly burnt pieces of toast, and a cup of light beer without sedatives, served in place of water. Because they were traveling through extremely dangerous waters where disaster could strike at any moment, Klein displayed the eating skills he had developed in college. Just as he had in the college mess hall, he finished breakfast in only a minute or two. He left the pirates' dining hall and went on deck, taking a post-meal stroll while observing his surroundings. At that moment, the sea still appeared as though it was illuminated by a midday sun as it was colored gold. Klein stopped and looked into the distance, where a point of light ahead was expanding. Under the sunlight, refraction caused the point of light to shimmer with a multicolored luster like a gigantic transparent gemstone. As the Future continued forging ahead, the point of light gradually revealed itself. It first split apart before becoming clear: four gigantic columns made of pure diamond. They resembled legendary pillars supporting the sea, extending downward as they stood firm and held up a sizable floating island. The floating island's soil was charred black, without a trace of greenery. In its depths, lights shone with such unnatural brilliance that they outshone the midday sky. Suddenly, a long screech rang out from the island. It was loud and unrestrained, but it gave people a hair-raising sense of danger. Before long, Klein heard galloping hooves and saw two steeds seemingly forged from gold rush out from the floating island. Behind them was a beautiful chariot likewise made of gold. At that moment, Cattleya hurriedly amplified her voice, making it resound throughout every corner of the Future. "Look down! "Don't look at it!" Klein was never one to put on a brave front. He subconsciously lowered his head upon hearing those words and looked at his leather boots. He noticed the sunlight illuminating the deck grow brighter before dimming and rapidly returning to its former brilliance. "It's all right now." Cattleya's voice sounded throughout the ship again, devoid of any obvious emotion. Only then did Klein look up. The two steeds forged from gold and the beautiful chariot they pulled had vanished. The diamond pillars silently supported the floating island as resplendent light swirled around it. What a huge diamond... What a strange floating island. What would happen if I hadn't lowered my head and watched the golden chariot charge forward? Klein looked around as he suddenly frowned. A pirate who had stood seven or eight meters away had vanished. In his place were two pitch-black footprints. Looking at the ashes floating in midair, Klein vaguely knew the outcome of not lowering his head. Thankfully, Admiral of Stars has been here a few times in the past. She knows what to avoid and when to bow her head. If I hired Mr. Hanged Man, even if he was the one steering the ghost ship, we might've already been wiped out by now... No, if the Future hadn't arrived at its destination ahead of time without giving me any time to prepare, I would've long sought out Will Auceptin's advice. A magician never performs unprepared... Besides, if I hired Mr. Hanged Man, I definitely would've purchased the relevant information from Ma'am Hermit... Klein first sighed before recovering his calm. He didn't suggest exploring the floating island. He let the Future sail past it and continue onward. For the rest of the time, the sea resembled the outside world. There were only undulating waves, vastness, silence, and an endless horizon. Klein occasionally saw fire embers floating on the surface of the sea, but he didn't find any signs of marine creatures, including mermaids. Time ticked by, and lunch was soon underway. Just as Klein was about to leave the deck for the dining hall, he suddenly realized that his surroundings had darkened! The sky, which had remained fixed at midday, lost all sunlight and became shrouded in profound darkness. The change was so abrupt that Klein's first reaction was to wonder who had switched off the lights! Silently, the Future was covered in a layer of resplendent stars that illuminated paths in every direction. Cattleya's magnetically alluring voice was magnified once again, resounding in everyone's ears. "Return to your room or find any corner you can and go to sleep. "Then, wait until you wake up naturally." Puzzled, Frank Lee asked loudly, "What will happen if I don't go to sleep?" At that moment, his voice boomed like a speaking bear. Cattleya stood behind the window of the captain's cabin and said, "When we wake up, we will find you gone, never to be found again." The night here is that terrifying? Klein was curious, but had no intention of trying to stay awake. He returned to his room and, using the starlight that still shone aboard the Future, unfolded a paper crane and picked up a pencil to quickly write: "What should I watch out for when traveling through the dangerous waters at the easternmost reaches of the Sonia Sea? "Where can I find mermaids there?" Putting down the pencil, he folded the crane. Without taking off his coat, he lay in bed and, with the help of Cogitation, quickly fell asleep. In a hazy world, he suddenly jolted awake, clearly knowing that he was dreaming. No one is infiltrating it... Klein surveyed his surroundings and found himself on a mountaintop. Behind and to either side of him were black, cloister-like buildings. Ahead stood a withered tree and a protruding boulder. Atop the boulder, Cattleya sat alone, hugging her knees and leaning forward as she stared at the mountain opposite them. She was still dressed in the classical black robe that exuded an air of mystery. Her face bore an indescribable look of confusion. At that moment, she didn't move at all; it was as though she was a stone sculpture. Why is she in my dream? Klein took a few steps forward and leaped onto a boulder. Before he could ask, the vast scene before his eyes stunned him, striking both body and soul. Before the boulder was a bottomless cliff, and across the chasm stood a mountain covered in countless palaces, spires, and majestic city walls. The opulent buildings were arranged in concentric tiers. Each one was abnormally huge and bore no resemblance to a human dwelling. Together, they possessed an indescribably epic grandeur, as though they belonged to legend or myth. The sun hung in the distance, casting the colors of sunset over the city in light that seemed frozen. "This is a dream shared by all of us..." Still sitting there with her knees hugged to her chest, Cattleya spoke as though in a reverie.
Chapter 649: Black Cloister A dream shared by everyone? Klein repeated Cattleya's words inwardly as he slowly realized the situation he was in. Nighttime in these dangerous waters would connect the dreams of all living creatures! Any creature that didn't sleep would lack the necessary protection, as its Soul Body wouldn't be in the dream. As such, it would suffer an unknown attack. As for why such an attack would lead to one's disappearance and not instant death, Klein, who hadn't actually experienced it, had no grounds for speculation. As his thoughts raced, Klein withdrew his gaze from Cattleya and turned it back toward the magnificent city across the cliff. He wondered curiously, If this world is truly formed by connecting the dreams of every creature here, whose mind could have conceived such an unimaginable city? He observed for a few seconds before asking, "What is its name?" What's the name of this city that can only exist in myths and legends? Cattleya stared ahead blankly and spoke as though in a reverie. "I don't know... We have a chance of seeing it each time we enter the dream, but it's impossible to approach. "She said that it resembles the Great Twilight Hall in Feysac. "She likely has her own guesses, but she has never told me." She? Queen Mystic? The Great Twilight Hall is the papal seat of the Church of the God of Combat... Klein surveyed the area and deliberated before saying, "I plan to look around." He believed the Future wouldn't leave these waters anytime soon. He would definitely experience more nights and enter this dream world several more times. Therefore, to guard against accidents and gather intelligence, he needed to explore the area. And such exploration undoubtedly required a partner. Cattleya remained seated, hugging her knees. In the same ethereal tone, she said, "I'm not interested." This isn't how a mature pirate admiral should speak. You could've been more tactful. Ma'am Hermit, you resemble a petulant young lady... Klein was taken aback and wondered whether he had misheard. This conflicted with his impression of Admiral of Stars. Remembering that Gehrman Sparrow also had a side that didn't fear dirt or hardship, he came to a realization and quickly formed a hypothesis. Cattleya isn't completely awake in the dream. She knows that she's in a dream, but she's unable to effectively control it! In other words, she would unconsciously reveal the feelings buried deep in her heart and aspects of her personality that she usually suppressed. No wonder she said that she was never able to approach that miraculous city. It's because she never had the intention of exploring it herself... Klein thought for a moment and deliberately probed, "We might be able to discover something over there." "I'm not going," Cattleya replied without hesitation, though she didn't shake her head. "I'll wait here! Wait!" She really is in a semi-unconscious state... Klein made the judgment based on her reaction and tone. He didn't waste any more time and turned to leap off the boulder. Thud! Klein landed on the ground and subconsciously looked back. Cattleya remained seated there, hugging her knees. No one else was around. The frozen sunset over the city opposite her cast a long shadow behind her, which blended with one of the shadows cast by the withered trees. A gentle mountain breeze blew, causing the dark silhouette to sway slightly. Cattleya didn't move as she stubbornly waited on the spot. At times like this, a Psychiatrist is needed to interpret the dream's emotions. This has nothing to do with revelations obtained through divination... Klein curled his lips and surveyed his surroundings, seeking a direction to explore. He discovered that no matter which direction he took, he would end up at the black cloister buildings. A towering wall separated them from the cliff. No matter how one explored, one had to pass through the cloister unless one jumped off the cliff. Since there was no other choice, Klein went directly to the pitch-black door of the cloister. The door was nearly ten meters tall and didn't look as though it had been made for humans. Klein sized it up for a few seconds, took a deep breath, and extended his hands to push against both sides. A creak followed. The door was far heavier than Klein had imagined. His muscles bulged and his face flushed red, yet he managed to move it only a fraction without pushing it open. Thankfully, it's only a dream. As long as I have reason to believe it, I can increase my strength without truly activating Creeping Hunger... Klein exhaled and made his left glove turn pale. In the midst of dark green sparkles, he obtained a Zombie's strength. His arm turned thicker as his legs swelled. Screech! A deep grinding sound boomed as the door slowly opened to reveal its interior. Two dark spires and the black buildings were connected by covered bridges, surrounding a vast square paved in gray stone. The square was riddled with holes in which enormous arrows were embedded. Burning piles stood in various places, as though the square had once come under attack. Klein passed through the gateway and entered the square. Unsurprisingly, he saw Frank Lee, Nina, Ottolov, and company there. Is this their dream? It doesn't seem like it... Or is everyone's dream confined to themselves, after which they're randomly placed somewhere in this world? Klein guessed without confidence. Frank Lee was the closest to him. He was holding a shovel and digging at some rubble. Beside him were the white bread, toast, and roasted fish which had previously fallen to the floor. He plans to use them as fertilizer? He's planting things even in his dreams... Klein walked over and casually asked, "What are you doing?" Frank didn't stop, but he revealed a smile. "I'm cultivating some little things. They need to sleep in the soil for a while before they can grow large and reproduce." "What's their use?" Klein asked, both worried and curious. Frank beamed and said, "They're a hybrid fungus. It can make bulls produce milk. That way, we can obtain more milk and allow more people to drink good milk." Spare those bulls... Klein's face twitched as he asked, "Will it succeed?" "There are no problems with the effects, but I'm very worried that they can't reproduce," Frank said with a frown. May Death forever favor them... Klein prayed as he walked past Frank Lee and headed for the black building's entrance across the square. Along the way, he passed by Nina and Navigator Ottolov, who were drinking beside a collapsed pillar. "Have you ever thought about leaving the pirate crew when you're older, finding a man to marry, and settling down? I don't think anyone wants to drift at sea their entire life." Ottolov removed his pointed bonnet, revealing slightly graying hair. His gaze and tone told Klein that the implication was: If that's what you want, why not consider me? Mr. Navigator, you're old enough to be Nina's father. You need to consider your health... As he passed, Klein couldn't help lampooning the conversation inwardly. Nina gulped a mouthful of beer and looked in a particular direction. "No, that's not the life I wish to lead. "Before joining you, I once tried settling down on Feysac's eastern coast and giving up piracy, but I couldn't bear the boredom. I had to haul wood and move things every day, and I could only stay home at night. I wasn't allowed to go to bars or hunt in the wilderness. That kind of life was always the same! Furthermore, I had to endure all kinds of criticism and put up with those irritating people. Even when I wanted to beat them up, I had to worry about the police! "Life is still better on the ship. Although it's boring most of the time, we often visit different places and encounter different things. Heh heh. Even during the dullest periods, I can torment those fellows and train them into passable pirates. I can also tell them that whoever performs best each month can spend the night in my room. Then, I'll watch them eagerly endure the torment. Of course, spending the night and having sex are two different things. It depends on my mood." A true female pirate... Everyone wants something different... Klein made a neutral assessment and saw nothing wrong with Nina's ideas. I won't object to her choice, but if she frequently murders, commits arson, and plunders, I won't mind exchanging her head for a bounty the next time we meet... Klein retracted his gaze and arrived at what appeared to be the entrance to the black buildings and spires. Subconsciously, he turned his head and realized that the shadows in the corner seemed normal, but something about them seemed different. Bloodless Heath Doyle? He hides in the shadows even in a dream? According to my limited knowledge of psychology, this is the result of a profound lack of security... Klein pushed against another door that was likewise nearly ten meters tall. Amidst the grinding sounds, his gaze suddenly froze. Behind the door was a vast hall which had two rows of stone pillars supporting it. The hall was abnormally dark, without a single candle. As the main door opened, light streamed in from outside and illuminated the interior. Klein saw murals in various colors covering the dome, predominantly gold. They connected seamlessly, giving him a sense of magnificence and sanctity. Thump! Thump! Thump! A figure stood with its back to Klein, using an axe to chop at a huge, long tree for some unknown purpose. The figure was dressed in a white shirt and a black vest. It didn't look like any of the pirates on the ship. There's someone else in these waters? Or could this be the owner of the mysterious eyes that had been observing the deck and me? Klein's heart sank as he slowed. He approached warily and moved to the figure's side, where he could see him clearly. He was a young-looking man with short blond hair parted thirty-seventy. His emerald-green eyes appeared focused and serious. "What are you doing? What is this place?" Klein asked cautiously. He intuitively believed that the person wasn't the owner of the mysterious eyes. The young man raised his hand to touch his earlobes without turning his head. "Why are you asking these questions? My ship sank, and I'm busy making myself a canoe. I don't have time to talk to you." Klein thought for a moment before asking, "Who are you?" "Who am I? I'm the unlucky Anderson. Ever since I saw that mural, I've been plagued with bad luck." The young man pointed in a direction. Tracing his finger, Klein saw a mural. The mural depicted a sea of fire that split in the middle to produce a path. A long line of people traveled along the path. Some bowed their heads in pious devotion, while others prostrated themselves on the ground. Their destination lay in the depths of the sea. Their leader was a lanky man with long silver hair. His features were gentle, his eyes tightly closed, and layers of wings covered his back. This... Klein's pupils constricted suddenly. He recognized the leader on the mural! It was the Angel of Fate which Little Sun had once depicted! It was the Tail Devourer, Ouroboros!
Chapter 650: The Unlucky Anderson After recognizing the leader on the mural, Klein subconsciously suspected that it was something from his dream. However, he quickly rejected the idea. The unlucky Anderson wasn't someone he knew, nor had the man ever left an impression on him. It was unlikely that Anderson was a product of his own dream. Furthermore, Anderson had clearly said that his bad luck began after he saw the mural. Since he was so strongly connected to it, the mural could only be part of Anderson's dream! Focusing on it, Klein quickly realized that this mural differed somewhat from the one Little Sun had seen in the True Creator's abandoned temple. The background here was a sea burning with golden flames, while the previous mural had depicted a desolate plain. Here, the destination was in the depths of the sea, while the previous path led toward a distant mountain. On the mountaintop stood a huge cross with a figure hanging upside down. Beneath the Angel of Fate Ouroboros's feet was black sludge, with heads hanging downward and fish trapped within. Previously, there had been a meandering river. It's a different mural, but more like a memory of another stage in the same pilgrimage... Klein nodded as he formed a hypothesis. A similar scene surfaced in his mind. A very long time ago, at some point during the Fourth Epoch, Ouroboros led a devout group of pilgrims, perhaps remnants of the True Creator's believers. Pursued by many powerful enemies, they sailed through this sea. For some reason, "He" abandoned the boat. With the help of the True Creator or "His" own powers, "He" parted the sea and led the devotees through it into the Forsaken Land of the Gods, leaving behind the seeds of organizations such as Rose Redemption and the Aurora Order. In the Forsaken Land of the Gods, they crossed desolate plains and built temples along their pilgrimage. One of those temples was discovered by Little Sun and his companions. Given how Will Auceptin was forced to restart a cycle and be reborn as a baby, the Tail Devourer is likely still alive... Does this mean that "He" eventually reached the destination with the pilgrims--the True Creator's holy residence? Does that mean the True Creator's holy residence is somewhere in the Forsaken Land of the Gods? At this thought, Klein suddenly felt an inexplicable sense of melancholy. If my theory is correct, then no matter how the City of Silver tries to save itself or pass on the flame, once the True Creator fully awakens or returns to "His" original state, they will inevitably be destroyed! When you're so close to an evil god's divine kingdom or holy residence, survival has nothing to do with how hard you struggle! They're like bubbles formed when waves surge onto the shore. Once the waves recede, they vanish. Human civilizations and peoples are simply that fragile beneath the gaze of an evil god. No, I can't be that pessimistic. This is only a hypothesis. Perhaps it wasn't Ouroboros who forced Will Auceptin to reincarnate. Perhaps the True Creator won't recover or awaken so easily. "He" might be sealed by the seven deities... Therefore, the City of Silver still has a chance. They need to open a path between the Forsaken Land of the Gods and the outside world before the evil god escapes "His" shackles, allowing everyone to evacuate! This is probably why the City of Silver's Chief released the Shepherd elder. They need to use every bit of power available to them... Klein forcibly reined in his thoughts. He suddenly felt uneasy, afraid that merely arriving here had trapped him in an endless cycle of fate created by the Tail Devourer. At this point, he instinctively wanted to take four steps counterclockwise and go above the gray fog. He wished to forcibly search for any memories he might have lost, but ultimately resisted the impulse and decided to observe first. According to his interpretation of the symbols, there were no looping rivers, only black sludge with fish embedded in it. This didn't signify a cycle of fate, only lingering bad luck! This was identical to what Anderson said! As a King of Angels, Ouroboros definitely possesses more than the power to cycle fate. Different temples have different murals, so depicting different powers is entirely logical... Besides, this is a dream! Besides, even if I did nothing and became trapped in a repeating cycle, forcing me to converse with the Admiral of Stars and make the same observations over and over, the problem would be exposed on Monday. The Tarot Club wouldn't be held, so Miss Justice and the others would become suspicious and pray. I could use their prayers to recover my memories... Klein instantly regained his confidence, though the chaos and tension in his heart were merely buried rather than gone. He looked ahead and discovered that the hall extended endlessly into the distance. Light shone only near the entrance; everything else was dark, growing darker the deeper it went. All he could see were wooden doors on both sides, with no indication of where they led. At the sight of this dark and eerie scene, Klein's desire to continue exploring dwindled. To encounter a mural left behind by a King of Angels here, who knows what will happen if I delve deeper or enter some room... Fear of the unknown was an ancient instinct. Premonitions of danger from unseen sources had given rise to a profound terror of the unknown. Klein examined his feelings for a few seconds and went no farther. He turned toward Anderson, who was chopping the gigantic tree. "Why are you here?" Anderson looked up and scoffed. "I'm a treasure hunter. "So tell me, why would I be here?" Treasure hunter... Klein casually asked, "Is there treasure here?" Anderson continued working on the so-called canoe. His voice suddenly turned deep. "There is treasure everywhere in these waters. "As long as you can claim it and leave alive." That's true... The problem is that this place is extremely dangerous for anyone who isn't a demigod, but even more dangerous for demigods... Klein looked into the depths of the hall and asked, "Do you know where this place is?" Anderson followed his gaze and said, "I don't know. "At least a third of my companions formed a team and went inside to explore, but they never returned." "Are you referring to the real world or the dream world?" Klein asked, his thoughts perfectly clear. Bang! After the axe landed, Anderson laughed. "Of course it's in the real world. "Another third of my companions went to explore the dream. They didn't return either." Klein inhaled sharply and fell into thought. "Where are their bodies in the real world?" "They mutated into monsters and killed quite a few of my companions." Anderson raised his axe and swung it down. Clang! With a crisp crack, his axe split in two. Because the fracture ran toward the back of the axe, a fragment immediately shot toward him. Blood immediately gushed from the right side of Anderson's chest and abdomen. He held his left hand to his wound and looked up at Klein. Smiling bitterly, he said, "I told you I was plagued with bad luck ever since I saw that mural. "Thankfully, this isn't considered too unlucky. At the very least, they didn't destroy my exceptionally handsome face." ...Is that really the right adjective to use? Klein watched Anderson swiftly pull the fragment from his body, treat the wound, and take some medicine. Anderson remained unfazed, and the practiced ease of his movements showed that he had long since grown accustomed to such mishaps. With one hand in his pocket, Klein toyed with the coins inside. After some deliberation, he asked, "When your companions began exploring, were you part of the group that stayed behind to study the mural?" Anderson was taken aback as he tucked his medicine pouch into his belt and wiped his mouth. "No. "I was part of the group that went exploring..." As he spoke, he grinned and revealed a genial smile. This... Klein's pupils constricted as he bent forward slightly and raised his left palm. At that moment, blinding sunlight turned everything dazzling white. Then, it dimmed and vanished. Klein opened his eyes naturally and discovered that the world outside had returned to its midday state. He took out the pocket watch in his inner pocket and opened it. Only half an hour has passed. The night here is rather short... That unlucky Anderson looked perfectly normal. Who would've known he was so terrifying! Rolling to his feet, Klein suddenly recalled something. Snake of Fate Will Auceptin had yet to "reply" to him! Was "He" unable to locate me because everyone's dreams had been drawn into a world disconnected from the spirit world? Or did "He" sense Ouroboros's aura and not dare approach? Or is there something inherently wrong with these waters? As his thoughts whirled, Klein decided to investigate. The method of verifying it was simple. He could go back to sleep while it was still "noon." However, he wasn't in a hurry because he didn't know whether there were any taboos against sleeping during the day. Wearing his cap, Klein went to the captain's cabin and knocked on the door. After three knocks, he retracted his hand and patiently waited. Before long, Cattleya opened the door. She no longer looked as lost as she had in the dream. She was wearing her thick glasses again. "Is it all right to sleep during the day?" Klein asked directly. Cattleya nodded. "Yes." After answering, she hesitated and asked, "You seemed very active in that dream?" Realizing how much danger lurked in these waters, and that he would inevitably be forced to reveal some of his abilities, Klein decided to lay the groundwork for future explanations. He looked at Cattleya and smiled politely. "Yes. "This is a gift bestowed upon me by my Lord." My Lord... Cattleya's eyes visibly shimmered behind her thick glasses. Unusually, she frowned slightly, then relaxed without asking any further questions. Klein thought for a moment, then he added, "Be careful of Heath Doyle." Cattleya clearly understood what he meant and answered directly, "Don't worry. He has a Sealed Artifact whose negative effect limits him to hearing only nearby voices." That's a clever use of a negative effect... Klein didn't belabor the point. He removed his hat and bowed before returning to his room. He lay down once again and used Cogitation to fall asleep. In the dream world, he woke up and saw the familiar pitch-black plains and black steeple. Phew, I can still establish a connection... Klein heaved a sigh of relief and entered the steeple. In the usual place, he saw the scattered tarot cards and the new words. "There are many dangers there, the greatest being the dream that begins when night falls. "The danger isn't simply that you'll disappear if you don't sleep, but there is one thing you must remember. "Do not explore that dream! "Absolutely do not explore that dream! "Since there's not enough space, I won't explain why. Alright, it's just a joke. The reason is that the area contains some of the dreams left behind by a deity."
